examples.source: we will use the spin-balanced variant of the UCJ ansatz
examples.suggested: فسنستخدم النسخة متوازنة السبين من نموذج UCJ
examples.translation: فسنستخدم المتغير متوازن السبين لنموذج UCJ
examples.why: ‘المتغيّر’ is the established Arabic word for *variable*; using it for ‘variant’ momentarily suggests a parameter rather than an alternative form of the ansatz. ‘النسخة’ or ‘الصيغة’ is the conventional rendering.

examples.source: The signal here comes from a priori knowledge of the electronic structure and molecular Hamiltonian.
examples.suggested: تأتي الإشارة هنا من المعرفة المسبقة بالبنية الإلكترونية وهاملتوني الجزيء.
examples.translation: تأتي الإشارة هنا من المعرفة المسبقة ببنية الإلكترونات وهاملتوني الجزيء.
examples.why: ‘electronic structure’ is a fixed term of art in quantum chemistry rendered ‘البنية الإلكترونية’; ‘بنية الإلكترونات’ (‘the structure of the electrons’) is a literal recasting that loses the term’s status as a named concept.

editor_note: The register (informal singular: شغِّل، راجع، برنامجك) and the kept-English brand terms are fine, but three renderings change the technical meaning. Worst: "zero-noise extrapolation (ZNE)" is rendered "الاستقراء عند تعامد الضوضاء" — literally "extrapolation at noise *orthogonality*"; the method has nothing to do with orthogonality, it extrapolates to the zero-noise limit (الاستقراء إلى الضوضاء الصفرية / عند انعدام الضوضاء), so a learner forms a false concept of the core error-mitigation technique named on this page. Second: "Parallelize classical tasks" becomes "موازنة المهام الكلاسيكية" (= *balancing* tasks) instead of "موازاة" (parallelizing) — a different capability from the one Qiskit Serverless is being sold on. Third: "optimizing for hardware" in the Application-functions workflow becomes "وتحسين الأجهزة" (= improving/optimizing *the hardware itself*) rather than optimizing the circuit for the hardware. Lesser: "readout mitigation" → "تخفيف قراءة المخرجات" drops "errors"; "Open Plan" is renamed "الخطة المجانية" (the Free Plan) while Premium/Flex/On-Prem are handled differently in the same file; "observables" → "مراقبات" (monitorings) rather than المرصودات/المؤثرات القابلة للقياس.

examples.source: readout mitigation and zero-noise extrapolation (ZNE) for error mitigation
examples.suggested: وتخفيف أخطاء القراءة والاستقراء إلى حد انعدام الضوضاء (ZNE) لتخفيف الأخطاء
examples.translation: وتخفيف قراءة المخرجات والاستقراء عند تعامد الضوضاء (ZNE) لتخفيف الأخطاء
examples.why: «تعامد الضوضاء» means "noise orthogonality" — ZNE is extrapolation to the ZERO-noise limit. The Arabic teaches a false concept of the technique. Also "readout mitigation" loses "errors": as written it says mitigating the readout, not its errors.

examples.source: Parallelize classical tasks, such as pre-processing and post-processing
examples.suggested: موازاة المهام الكلاسيكية، مثل المعالجة المسبقة واللاحقة
examples.translation: موازنة المهام الكلاسيكية، مثل المعالجة المسبقة واللاحقة
examples.why: «موازنة» = balancing/comparing, not parallelizing (موازاة). The bullet advertises a different capability from the English.

examples.source: entire quantum workflows, from mapping classical to quantum, optimizing for hardware, execution on hardware, and post-processing
examples.suggested: ... والتحسين بما يلائم الأجهزة، والتنفيذ على الأجهزة، ...
examples.translation: سير عمل الكم بأكمله، من تعيين الكلاسيكي إلى الكمي، وتحسين الأجهزة، والتنفيذ على الأجهزة، والمعالجة اللاحقة
examples.why: «تحسين الأجهزة» says the workflow step optimizes the hardware itself; the English means optimizing the circuit FOR the hardware — an inverted object in a step-by-step pedagogical list.

examples.source: Note that Open Plan users cannot submit session jobs.
examples.suggested: لاحظ أن مستخدمي خطة Open (الخطة المفتوحة) لا يمكنهم إرسال مهام الجلسات.
examples.translation: لاحظ أن مستخدمي الخطة المجانية لا يمكنهم إرسال مهام جلسات.
examples.why: Renames a proper plan ("Open Plan") to "the Free Plan"; the reader looking for this restriction in the console will not find a plan by that name, and the file keeps On-Prem in English while translating other plan names.

examples.source: take abstract circuits and desired measurement observables as input
examples.suggested: ... والمرصودات (observables) المطلوب قياسها كمدخلات
examples.translation: التي تأخذ الـ Circuits المجردة ومراقبات القياس المطلوبة كمدخلات
examples.why: «مراقبات» reads as "monitorings/supervisions", not the quantum observable; recognizable in context but not the conventional domain term.

examples.source: is a client for that service, and is the successor to the Qiskit IBM Provider
examples.suggested: هي العميل الخاص بتلك الخدمة، وهي الخليفة لحزمة Qiskit IBM Provider
examples.translation: هي عميل لتلك الخدمة، وخلف لـ Qiskit IBM Provider
examples.why: «وخلف لـ» is a bare calque of "successor to" that no native technical writer would use in this position; the elided copula makes the clause read as machine output.

editor_note: Nothing here would mislead a learner — the table marks, the note numbering and the substantive claims (ISA compilation requirement, no parsing of `duration`/`stretch` declarations, aliasing of classical registers strongly discouraged) all match the English faithfully, and the informal "ty" holds throughout ("najdeš", "Pokud OpenQASM 3 přímo nepoužíváš", "Nauč se", "Projdi si"). What a native technical editor would change is the handling of the kept-English terms: "circuit/circuits" is inserted undeclined into Czech syntax ("odesílání circuits", "vytvoření circuit", "dynamické circuits", "circuit boxy", "na platné ISA circuits"), and "Backend"/"Gate" are capitalized mid-sentence German-style and left uninflected ("daného Backend", "do ISA Backend", "na některých Backends", "parametry Gate", "modifikátory Gate") — Czech would write "backendu", "backendech", "hradel/bran" or at least lowercase, declined forms. Note 7 leaves the English adverb raw in Czech prose: "bude během parsování eagerly vyhodnocovat modifikátory Gate". Two qualifiers soften or harden: note 9's "can enable executing" becomes the flat assertion "umožňují spuštění" (dropped modal), and note 4's "supports outputting them" is pulled into the modal chain as "může … podporovat jejich výstup". Smaller grammar/calque slips: "ve Qiskit v2.1.0" (should be "v Qiskitu"), "unicode názvy" (English noun-adjunct order), "omezeného okruhu typů" for "restricted set of types", and mismatched quote marks („podporováno").

examples.source: will eagerly evaluate gate modifiers during the parse
examples.suggested: modifikátory hradel vyhodnotí okamžitě už během parsování
examples.translation: bude během parsování eagerly vyhodnocovat modifikátory Gate
examples.why: The English adverb "eagerly" is left untranslated inside Czech prose — a raw-MT artifact a Czech reader cannot parse as Czech; "Gate" is also capitalized and undeclined mid-sentence.

examples.source: Certain runtime configuration options can enable executing such circuits on some backends.
examples.suggested: Určité možnosti konfigurace za běhu mohou spuštění takových obvodů na některých backendech umožnit.
examples.translation: Určité možnosti konfigurace za běhu umožňují spuštění takových circuits na některých Backends.
examples.why: The hedge "can enable" is flattened to a plain assertion "umožňují" (they do enable), strengthening the claim right after the sentence saying such variables are not currently eligible for hardware execution.

examples.source: submitting circuits … create the circuit … suitable dynamic circuits hardware … circuit boxes … valid ISA circuits
examples.suggested: odesílání obvodů … vytvoření obvodu … hardwaru pro dynamické obvody … boxy obvodu … na platné ISA obvody
examples.translation: odesílání circuits … vytvoření circuit … hardwaru pro dynamické circuits … circuit boxy … na platné ISA circuits
examples.why: The English noun is dropped into Czech syntax without declension in every case, so it never agrees with its governing preposition; the file meanwhile does translate the neighbouring "registers" ("kvantové a klasické registry"), making the convention internally inconsistent.

examples.source: backend Instruction Set Architecture (ISA) … transpiled for a backend … the backend ISA … on some backends
examples.suggested: ISA daného backendu … transpilován pro backend … do ISA backendu … na některých backendech
examples.translation: ISA daného Backend … transpilován pro Backend … do ISA Backend … na některých Backends
examples.why: "Backend" is capitalized like a German noun and left uninflected, including the English plural "Backends"; Czech technical writing declines this loanword (backend/backendu/backendech) and keeps it lowercase.

examples.source: `for` loops in Qiskit v2.1.0 are not well supported.
examples.suggested: Smyčky `for` v Qiskitu v2.1.0 nejsou dobře podporovány.
examples.translation: Smyčky `for` ve Qiskit v2.1.0 nejsou dobře podporovány.
examples.why: "ve Qiskit" is doubly wrong: the vocalized preposition "ve" is not used before "Q", and the name is left undeclined; the same sentence pair also has "reprezentovány Qiskit" instead of instrumental "Qiskitem".

examples.source: unicode names / a restricted set of types
examples.suggested: názvy v Unicode / omezené sady typů
examples.translation: unicode názvy / omezeného okruhu typů
examples.why: "unicode názvy" copies English noun-adjunct order that Czech does not allow unadapted, and "okruh" (circle, sphere) is the wrong noun for a set of types — "sada"/"množina" is the term a Czech engineer would write.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout and the informal "du" holds consistently ("musst du in der Lage sein", "Betrachte die Wirkung", "Führe die Version ... aus"), so nothing here misleads a learner — but the Background section carries three renderings a native technical editor would change. In "Stabilisator-Codes konzentrieren sich kritisch auf die Korrektur eines diskreten Fehlersatzes mit Unterstützung aus der Pauli-Gruppe", the mathematical "support" (of an operator) becomes "Unterstützung" (help/backing) instead of "Träger"; "critically" becomes the false-friend calque "kritisch" instead of "entscheidend/vor allem"; and "error set" becomes "Fehlersatz", where German math uses "Menge", not "Satz" (= theorem). "Ancilla" is also split within the file: "zusätzliche Hilfs-Qubits" in Background vs "Stabilisatormessungs-Ancillas" in Step 1 — the concept stays identifiable, but the term should be unified. Minor stiffness in "mit [Visualisierung]-Unterstützung" (link-plus-hyphen calque of "with visualization support").

examples.source: Stabilizer codes critically focus on correcting a discrete error set with support from the Pauli group $\Pi^n$.
examples.suggested: Stabilisatorcodes zielen vor allem auf die Korrektur einer diskreten Fehlermenge, deren Träger in der Pauli-Gruppe $\Pi^n$ liegt.
examples.translation: Stabilisator-Codes konzentrieren sich kritisch auf die Korrektur eines diskreten Fehlersatzes mit Unterstützung aus der Pauli-Gruppe $\Pi^n$.
examples.why: Three problems in one sentence: mathematical 'support' (Träger) is rendered as 'Unterstützung' (= help/backing), which suggests the Pauli group assists the correction rather than containing the errors; 'critically' is the false-friend calque 'kritisch' instead of 'entscheidend/vor allem'; and 'error set' becomes 'Fehlersatz', where German mathematics says 'Menge' ('Satz' reads as theorem).

examples.source: additional ancilla qubits ... the remaining two are used as stabilizer measurement ancillas
examples.suggested: zusätzliche Ancilla-Qubits ... die verbleibenden zwei dienen als Ancillas für die Stabilisatormessung
examples.translation: zusätzliche Hilfs-Qubits ... die verbleibenden zwei werden als Stabilisatormessungs-Ancillas verwendet
examples.why: Within-file inconsistency: 'ancilla' is first Germanized to 'Hilfs-Qubits' and later kept as 'Ancillas' inside the heavy compound 'Stabilisatormessungs-Ancillas'. Either convention is defensible on its own, but the file should pick one; the compound would also read better split apart.

examples.source: Qiskit SDK v2.0 or later, with [visualization](...) support
examples.suggested: Qiskit SDK v2.0 oder neuer, mit Unterstützung für [Visualisierung](...)
examples.translation: Qiskit SDK v2.0 oder neuer, mit [Visualisierung](...)-Unterstützung
examples.why: Calqued English noun stacking: gluing '-Unterstützung' onto the closing bracket of a link produces a construction no German technical writer would put on the page; a prepositional phrase reads naturally and keeps the link intact.

editor_note: Nothing here misleads: the physics prose is faithful (measurement in the Pauli-$Z$ eigenbasis, 0/1 with probabilities $p_0$/$p_1$, measure_active covering only non-idle qubits 0 and 2), and informal "du" holds throughout ("kannst du es ... _messen_", "Nutze die Methode", "Erfahre, wie man Qubits misst"). Four things a native technical editor would still change: (1) the caveat in the Next-steps list, "(Available only when using Qiskit Runtime.)", is left entirely in English while the rest of the bullet list is German; (2) "computational basis" is rendered as the calque "Berechnungsbasis" instead of the conventional German "Rechenbasis"/"Standardbasis"; (3) the measure_active sentence "mit einer Größe gleich der Anzahl der nicht im Leerlauf befindlichen Qubits" is a word-for-word transfer of "with a size equal to the number of ..." that no German technical writer would produce (natural: "deren Größe der Anzahl ... entspricht"); (4) German compound hyphenation is missing throughout the headings and body — "Die Qiskit Klasse [Measure]", "`QuantumCircuit.measure` Methode", "`Measure` Klasse" should be "Qiskit-Klasse", "`QuantumCircuit.measure`-Methode", "`Measure`-Klasse". Core terminology (Qubit, Circuit, klassisches Bit, Messung, Eigenzustände) is correct and consistent.

examples.source: - [Mid-circuit measurements](/guides/execute-dynamic-circuits#midcircuit) (Available only when using Qiskit Runtime.)
examples.suggested: - [Messungen mitten im Circuit](/guides/execute-dynamic-circuits#midcircuit) (Nur bei Verwendung von Qiskit Runtime verfügbar.)
examples.translation: - [Mid-circuit measurements](/guides/execute-dynamic-circuits#midcircuit) (Available only when using Qiskit Runtime.)
examples.why: The restricting caveat is prose, not a code identifier, and is the only untranslated sentence on the page; a German-only reader loses the constraint that mid-circuit measurement requires Qiskit Runtime.

examples.source: In Qiskit, measurements are performed in the computational basis, that is, the single-qubit Pauli-$Z$ basis.
examples.suggested: In Qiskit werden Messungen in der Rechenbasis durchgeführt, das heißt in der Ein-Qubit-Pauli-$Z$-Basis.
examples.translation: In Qiskit werden Messungen in der Berechnungsbasis durchgeführt, das heißt, der Ein-Qubit-Pauli-$Z$-Basis.
examples.why: "Berechnungsbasis" is a literal calque; German quantum-computing texts use "Rechenbasis" (or "Standardbasis"). Recognizable, so MINOR, but not the established term.

examples.source: This method creates a new `ClassicalRegister` with a size equal to the number of non-idle qubits being measured.
examples.suggested: Diese Methode erstellt ein neues `ClassicalRegister`, dessen Größe der Anzahl der gemessenen, nicht im Leerlauf befindlichen Qubits entspricht.
examples.translation: Diese Methode erstellt ein neues `ClassicalRegister` mit einer Größe gleich der Anzahl der nicht im Leerlauf befindlichen Qubits, die gemessen werden.
examples.why: "mit einer Größe gleich der Anzahl" is a direct transfer of the English postmodifier; a German technical writer would use a relative clause with "entspricht". Meaning is intact, but it reads as machine output.

examples.source: The Qiskit [Measure](...) class measures the specified qubits.
examples.suggested: Die Qiskit-Klasse [Measure](...) misst die angegebenen Qubits.
examples.translation: Die Qiskit Klasse [Measure](...) misst die spezifizierten Qubits.
examples.why: Missing compound hyphen (also "`QuantumCircuit.measure` Methode", "`Measure` Klasse" in the headings), which is an orthography error in German, not a style choice; "spezifizierten" is an unnecessary latinate calque for "angegebenen".

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout and the informal "tú" register holds consistently (visita, Aprende, Consulta, instálalo, Ten en cuenta) — nothing here would mislead a learner. But the English word "circuits" is left untranslated twice in running prose ("ejecutar circuits cuánticos en procesadores cuánticos", "toman circuits abstractos"), where Spanish requires "circuitos"; this is a straight English leak, not a deliberate keep-in-English convention, since "circuito" is universal in Spanish quantum writing. "Primitives" is rendered as masculine "los primitivos / un primitivo", whereas the established Spanish domain term is feminine "las primitivas" ("primitivo" as a noun reads as "primitive/savage"); it is at least used consistently. The Qiskit Functions bullet labels are split three ways within four lines: "Funciones de Circuit" (half-translated), "las Circuit functions" (English), and "Funciones de aplicación" (fully translated) — pick one pattern. Finally, "run over a specified number of shots" becomes "que se puede ejecutar durante un número específico de shots", where "durante" reads as a time span rather than a count; "con un número determinado de shots" is the natural phrasing.

examples.source: executing quantum circuits on quantum processors / take abstract circuits and desired measurement observables as input
examples.suggested: al ejecutar circuitos cuánticos en procesadores cuánticos / que toman circuitos abstractos y los observables de medición deseados como entrada
examples.translation: al ejecutar circuits cuánticos en procesadores cuánticos / que toman circuits abstractos y los observables de medición deseados como entrada
examples.why: The English noun "circuits" is left untranslated in Spanish prose in two separate paragraphs, while the rest of the file translates ordinary technical nouns normally. "Circuito" is the universal Spanish domain term and there is no keep-in-English convention for it; as written it reads as an untranslated leak, and the adjective agreement ("circuits cuánticos") makes it look like a half-edited sentence.

examples.source: provides optimal implementations of Qiskit primitives ... A Job is a single query to a primitive
examples.suggested: proporciona implementaciones óptimas de las primitivas de Qiskit ... Un Job es una consulta única a una primitiva
examples.translation: proporciona implementaciones óptimas de los primitivos de Qiskit ... Un Job es una consulta única a un primitivo
examples.why: The conventional Spanish rendering of a computing "primitive" is the feminine noun "primitiva"; masculine "primitivo" as a standalone noun carries the everyday sense of "primitive/savage" and reads as a literal calque. It is at least internally consistent here, so this is a term-quality issue rather than a comprehension one.

examples.source: Circuit functions: ... With Circuit functions, users can ... / Application functions: ...
examples.suggested: **Funciones de circuito**: ... Con las funciones de circuito, los usuarios pueden ... / **Funciones de aplicación**: ...
examples.translation: **Funciones de Circuit**: ... Con las Circuit functions, los usuarios pueden ... / **Funciones de aplicación**: ...
examples.why: The same product-category name appears in three different forms within four lines — half-translated in the bold label, fully English in the body sentence, and fully translated for the sibling bullet. A reader scanning the two parallel bullets sees an inconsistent naming pattern where the English has a clean symmetry between "Circuit functions" and "Application functions".

examples.source: A Job is a single query to a primitive that can be run over a specified number of shots.
examples.suggested: Un Job es una consulta única a una primitiva que se puede ejecutar con un número determinado de shots.
examples.translation: Un Job es una consulta única a un primitivo que se puede ejecutar durante un número específico de shots.
examples.why: "Durante" renders English "over" literally and implies a duration in time, whereas shots are a count of repetitions; a native technical writer would use "con" (or "para") plus "un número determinado de shots". The meaning survives because "shots" is a countable noun, but the preposition is a visible calque.

editor_note: The central mechanism sentence mistranslates "quasiprobability distribution" as "التوزيع الاحتمالي شبه الكمومي" — the "شبه" (quasi-) is attached to "كمومي" (quantum, a word absent from the English), so the Arabic reads "the joint quasi-QUANTUM PROBABILITY distribution". That asserts the distribution is an ordinary probability distribution and invents a colliding real term (شبه كمومي = semi-quantum); it destroys the one concept the whole cutting addon rests on (QPD = quasi-probability decomposition, whose coefficients can be negative — the very reason for the $9^3$ sampling overhead discussed two sections later). It should be "التوزيع شبه الاحتمالي المشترك". Secondary, non-misleading issues: "shallower" is rendered "أكثر سطحيةً" (more superficial) instead of the natural "أقل عمقًا"; "gate" is split within the file between the kept-English "الـ Gates"/"قطع Gate" and the Arabic "بوابة" (line 92); and "arbitrarily chosen" is tightened to "مختارة عشوائيًا" (randomly chosen). Register is correctly informal throughout ("يمكنك توفير", "أعِد بناء", "ادمجها").

examples.source: many subexperiments are generated from the decomposed gates' joint quasiprobability distribution
examples.suggested: يُولَّد عدد كبير من التجارب الفرعية من التوزيع شبه الاحتمالي المشترك للـ Gates المُحلَّلة
examples.translation: يُولَّد عدد كبير من التجارب الفرعية من التوزيع الاحتمالي شبه الكمومي المشترك للـ Gates المحللة
examples.why: "quasi" is misattached to an invented "كمومي" (quantum). The learner is told this is a probability distribution that is "quasi-quantum" — a different, real term (semi-quantum) — and loses the actual concept of a quasiprobability distribution (values that may be negative), which is what QPD in this tutorial stands for and what makes the 9^3 sampling overhead necessary.

examples.source: Demonstrate that the QPD subexperiments will be shallower after cutting distant gates
examples.suggested: إثبات أن التجارب الفرعية لـ QPD ستكون أقل عمقًا بعد قطع الـ Gates البعيدة
examples.translation: إثبات أن التجارب الفرعية لـ QPD ستكون أكثر سطحيةً بعد قطع الـ Gates البعيدة
examples.why: سطحية carries the pejorative sense "superficial" in Arabic; for circuit depth a native technical writer writes أقل عمقًا, which also matches عمق used in the surrounding prose and in the printed depth values.

examples.source: one for each gate decomposition
examples.suggested: واحد لكل تحليل Gate (or convert the whole file to البوابات consistently)
examples.translation: واحد لكل تحليل بوابة (elsewhere: قطع الـ Gates البعيدة، ثلاثة CNOT Gates، title قطع Gate)
examples.why: "gate" is rendered as the kept-English "Gate/Gates" everywhere except this one spot, where it becomes بوابة; the title also uses an unidiomatic bare singular "قطع Gate" where "قطع الـ Gates" or "قطع البوابات" is expected.

examples.source: Here is an example of an arbitrarily chosen subexperiment generated from the QPD circuit.
examples.suggested: فيما يلي مثال على تجربة فرعية مختارة اعتباطيًا مُولَّدة من دائرة QPD.
examples.translation: فيما يلي مثال على تجربة فرعية مختارة عشوائيًا مُولَّدة من دائرة QPD.
examples.why: "arbitrarily" (any one will do, index 100 was picked by hand) becomes "randomly", implying a random draw in a section already dense with sampling language — a small but avoidable shift in a probabilistic context.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — no drift, no inverted conditions, no dropped caveats; informal "tú" holds consistently ("puedes usar", "tu cuenta", "consulta"), and IBM product names (IBM Cloud Logs Routing, Container Registry) are correctly left untranslated. The residual problems are stylistic calques a native technical editor would rewrite: "Los siguientes campos están incluidos en el registro" is a stiff English passive where Spanish would say "El registro incluye los siguientes campos", and "Para información sobre..." (twice, lines 32 and 36) is a direct calque of "For information about..." instead of "Para obtener información sobre". There is also a small within-file lexical split: "log" is rendered "registro" everywhere except "instancia de log de flujo" in the logSourceCRN row, which should read "instancia de registro de flujo" for consistency. None of this misleads a learner.

examples.source: The following fields are included in the log record.
examples.suggested: El registro incluye los siguientes campos.
examples.translation: Los siguientes campos están incluidos en el registro.
examples.why: Calqued English passive; Spanish technical prose prefers the active construction with the record as subject. Also drops the nuance of "log record" vs. plain "registro".

examples.source: For information about launching the IBM Cloud Logs interface, see ... / For information about fields included in every platform log, see ...
examples.suggested: Para obtener información sobre cómo abrir la interfaz de IBM Cloud Logs, consulta ... / Para obtener información sobre los campos incluidos ...
examples.translation: Para información sobre cómo abrir la interfaz de IBM Cloud Logs, consulta ... / Para información sobre los campos incluidos en cada registro de plataforma, consulta ...
examples.why: "Para información sobre" is a direct transposition of "For information about"; native Spanish documentation (including IBM's own) uses "Para obtener información sobre" or "Para más información sobre".

examples.source: Defines the account and flow log instance where the log is published.
examples.suggested: Define la cuenta y la instancia de registro de flujo donde se publica el registro.
examples.translation: Define la cuenta y la instancia de log de flujo donde se publica el registro.
examples.why: The file consistently renders "log" as "registro" (registros de plataforma, instancias de registro, registro que se genera); this single row switches to the English "log", making the same concept look like two different things.

examples.source: The following table lists the locations where the automatic collection of Container Registry service logs is enabled.
examples.suggested: En la siguiente tabla se enumeran las ubicaciones donde está habilitada la recopilación automática de registros del servicio Container Registry.
examples.translation: La siguiente tabla lista las ubicaciones donde está habilitada la recopilación automática de registros del servicio Container Registry.
examples.why: Transitive "listar" mirroring English "lists" reads as translationese; "enumerar" or "mostrar" is the idiomatic verb in Spanish documentation. Defensible but not what a native writer would produce.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — no inversions, no swapped quantities, the CNOT condition ("uniquement lorsque le premier qubit est |1⟩"), the ⟨ZZI⟩=1 explanation, the 2-qubit-depth n→n/2 claim and the teleportation summary (no-cloning, no faster-than-light transfer) all match the English — and the informal "tu" convention holds with zero vous/votre/veuillez slips. The main defect is that "gate" is split within the file between correct French "porte" and a leaked, capitalized English "Gate" used as a French noun: headings read "### Gate X", "### Gate H", "### Gate CX (Gate CNOT)" and the body "Une Gate Hadamard", "l'application d'une Gate X", "plus de 1000 Gates", "une séquence de gates CNOT en escalier", "la profondeur des gates à 2 qubits", "les gates à qubit unique" — while the very same passages elsewhere correctly say "une porte X", "la porte NOT contrôlée", "des portes quantiques", "les portes de base", "la profondeur en portes à deux qubits". "Rotation gates" is left as an untranslated English noun phrase inside French syntax ("une combinaison de rotation gates $R_y$", "à l'aide de rotation gates") instead of "portes de rotation". Secondary: "job"/"tâche" are split (four paragraphs use "tâche", then "du résultat du job" and "Soumets le job"); the encoding terms are half-translated (heading "## 3.1 Encodage en amplitude" but body "l'amplitude encoding", and "## 3.2 Angle encoding et circuits paramétrés" untranslated); "Backend" is capitalized as a proper noun mid-sentence ("l'ISA de ce Backend", "un Backend quantique"); the H1 "# 1. Portes Quantiques et circuits Quantiques" copies English title case onto French adjectives; and "the open plan" gains an unsourced gloss as "le plan Open (gratuit)".

examples.source: ### X Gate / ### H Gate / ### CX Gate (CNOT Gate)
examples.suggested: ### Porte X / ### Porte H / ### Porte CX (porte CNOT)
examples.translation: ### Gate X / ### Gate H / ### Gate CX (Gate CNOT)
examples.why: The section headings keep the English noun "Gate" while the body of the very same sections says "Une porte X" and "La porte NOT contrôlée" — the core domain term is split within one file. French quantum writing uses "porte" unambiguously.

examples.source: A Hadamard gate represents... / equivalent to applying an X gate / over 1000 gates / a staircase-like CNOT gates sequence / 2-qubit gate depth ... single qubit gates
examples.suggested: Une porte de Hadamard... / d'une porte X / plus de 1000 portes / une séquence de portes CNOT en escalier / la profondeur en portes à 2 qubits ... les portes à un seul qubit
examples.translation: Une Gate Hadamard représente... / équivalent à l'application d'une Gate X / plus de 1000 Gates / une séquence de gates CNOT en escalier / la profondeur des gates à 2 qubits ... les gates à qubit unique
examples.why: "Gate" is inflected as a French noun ("une Gate", "1000 Gates") in the same paragraphs that elsewhere write "les portes de base" and "la profondeur en portes à deux qubits". Recognizable, so not misleading, but a native technical editor would unify on "porte".

examples.source: This state can be prepared using a combination of rotation gates $R_y$ ... / Hence we have seen how to encode information using rotational gates.
examples.suggested: ... une combinaison de portes de rotation $R_y$ ... / ... à l'aide de portes de rotation.
examples.translation: Cet état peut être préparé en utilisant une combinaison de rotation gates $R_y$ ... / On a donc vu comment encoder des informations à l'aide de rotation gates.
examples.why: "rotation gates" is an untranslated English noun phrase dropped into French syntax with English modifier order; a French-speaking quantum engineer would write "portes de rotation".

examples.source: through the job result's PubResult.data.evs ... / Submit the job and if you execute it on hardware
examples.suggested: ... du résultat de la tâche / Soumets la tâche ...
examples.translation: via les attributs PubResult.data.evs ... du résultat du job / Soumets le job et si tu l'exécutes sur du matériel réel
examples.why: The surrounding paragraphs consistently render "job" as "tâche" ("Soumets une tâche en utilisant la primitive Estimator", "Après la fin de la tâche"), then switch to English "job" twice — an in-file split of the same term.

examples.source: Make sure to choose the open plan.
examples.suggested: Assure-toi de choisir le plan Open.
examples.translation: Assure-toi de choisir le plan Open (gratuit).
examples.why: "(gratuit)" is added and has no counterpart in the English. It happens to be true of the Open plan, so it does not mislead, but the translation should not inject product claims the source does not make.

examples.source: # 1. Quantum Gates and Quantum Circuits / ## 3.1 Amplitude encoding / ## 3.2 Angle encoding and parametrized circuits
examples.suggested: # 1. Portes quantiques et circuits quantiques / ## 3.1 Encodage en amplitude / ## 3.2 Encodage en angle et circuits paramétrés
examples.translation: # 1. Portes Quantiques et circuits Quantiques / ## 3.1 Encodage en amplitude / ## 3.2 Angle encoding et circuits paramétrés
examples.why: English title-case is copied onto French adjectives ("Portes Quantiques"), and the two encoding headings are handled inconsistently — 3.1 translated, 3.2 left in English — while the conclusion mixes both ("l'amplitude encoding et l'angle encoding").

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — no drift, no inverted conditions, all quantities intact (50 qubits, 100 qubits, 15 mai 2024, 0.22.0, Open-Plan job/batch restriction), and domain terminology is correct and internally consistent (qubits, portes de base, carte de couplage, backends factices, transpiler and snapshots kept in English, ansatz untranslated, circuits de Clifford vs circuits stabilisateurs correctly distinguished). The "tu" convention holds with no vous/votre slips. What a native editor would still change: (1) "Ce processus est mieux réalisé par l'expérimentation directe" is a calqued passive for "This process is best achieved through…" — a French technical writer would write "Le meilleur moyen d'y parvenir est l'expérimentation directe"; (2) in the local-testing-mode note, the contrastive "Instead" is dropped entirely and "de suppression ou de mitigation des erreurs intégrée" leaves the adjective agreeing with only the second noun; (3) "gagner en confiance dans une expérience" reads as self-confidence rather than the EN sense of trusting the experiment's results ("renforcer la confiance dans une expérience"). None of these would mislead a learner.

examples.source: This process is best achieved through direct experimentation with quantum hardware.
examples.suggested: Le meilleur moyen d'y parvenir est d'expérimenter directement avec du matériel quantique.
examples.translation: Ce processus est mieux réalisé par l'expérimentation directe avec du matériel quantique.
examples.why: Word-for-word rendering of the English passive superlative. Grammatical but stiff — French technical prose fronts the recommendation rather than saying a process 'est mieux réalisé par'.

examples.source: Local testing mode does not have built-in error suppression or mitigation.  Instead, you must specify those options explicitly.
examples.suggested: Le mode de test local ne dispose pas de suppression ni de mitigation des erreurs intégrées. Tu dois donc spécifier ces options explicitement.
examples.translation: Le mode de test local ne dispose pas de suppression ou de mitigation des erreurs intégrée. Tu dois spécifier ces options explicitement.
examples.why: The contrastive connective 'Instead' is dropped, so the two sentences merely sit side by side instead of the second answering the first; and 'intégrée' agrees only with 'mitigation', leaving 'suppression' dangling. Meaning survives, but the emphasis flattens.

examples.source: results can be verified, which is a useful way to gain confidence in an experiment
examples.suggested: …ce qui est un moyen utile de renforcer la confiance dans une expérience
examples.translation: les résultats peuvent être vérifiés, ce qui est un moyen utile de gagner en confiance dans une expérience
examples.why: 'gagner en confiance' in French idiomatically means the person becomes more self-assured; the English means trusting the experiment's results. The pedagogical point (verifiability builds trust in the experiment) is slightly blurred.

editor_note: Three prose statements say something the English does not, and each would mislead a learner. (1) The matrix-multiplication sentence replaces the English "can be performed using the `@` operator" with "באמצעות הפונקציה `matmul` מ-`NumPy`" — the code cell immediately below uses `M1 @ ket1`, so the sentence no longer describes its own example and the operator the lesson is teaching is never named. (2) The `Operator.draw` note says the `latex` option is equivalent to `array_from_latex` instead of `array_to_latex` — a non-existent function name, and the inverted direction (from/to) is exactly what a beginner would copy. (3) "global phase" is rendered "שלב גלובלי" (= global *stage/step*) rather than the standard "פאזה גלובלית", so the sentence about vectors being equivalent up to a global phase teaches a false concept and the emphasised term *שוות ערך עד שלב גלובלי* is unidentifiable to a Hebrew reader who later meets "פאזה". Secondary (non-misleading) issues: the idiom "leaves something to be desired" is calqued as the broken "מניח מה לרצות" (should be "מותיר מה לרצות"); "circuit" is split within the file between "מעגל קוונטי" (headings, line 302) and bare English "Circuit" ("ניתן להגדיר Circuit קוונטי", "ל-Circuit זה", "מה-Circuit"); and "unitary" is split between "פעולות אוניטריות" and the ungrammatical "מטריצת היוניטרי" (should be "המטריצה האוניטרית").

examples.source: Matrix multiplication, including matrix-vector multiplication as a special case, can be performed using the `@` operator.
examples.suggested: כפל מטריצות, כולל כפל מטריצה-וקטור כמקרה פרטי, ניתן לבצע באמצעות האופרטור `@`.
examples.translation: כפל מטריצות, כולל כפל מטריצה-וקטור כמקרה פרטי, ניתן לבצע באמצעות הפונקציה `matmul` מ-`NumPy`.
examples.why: Substitutes a different API for the one the lesson teaches; the code cell directly below uses `@`, so the sentence no longer matches its own example and the `@` operator is never introduced.

examples.source: they are said to be *equivalent up to a global phase* because one is equal to the other multiplied by a complex number on the unit circle.
examples.suggested: אומרים שהן *שקולות עד כדי פאזה גלובלית* מכיוון שאחת שווה לשנייה כפול מספר מרוכב על מעגל היחידה.
examples.translation: אומרים שהן *שוות ערך עד שלב גלובלי* מכיוון שאחת שווה לשנייה כפול מספר מרוכב על מעגל היחידה.
examples.why: 'phase' is rendered as שלב (stage/step) instead of the physics term פאזה. The core concept of a global phase becomes unrecognisable and the learner forms a false idea (a 'stage' rather than a complex unit-modulus factor); 'עד כדי' is also the correct Hebrew for 'up to'.

examples.source: Note that the `latex` option produces results equivalent to `array_to_latex`.
examples.suggested: שים לב שאפשרות `latex` מייצרת תוצאות שוות ערך ל-`array_to_latex`.
examples.translation: שים לב שאפשרות `latex` מייצרת תוצאות שוות ערך ל-`array_from_latex`.
examples.why: The function name is inverted to a non-existent `array_from_latex`; the reader is pointed at an API that does not exist and the array→LaTeX direction is reversed.

examples.source: This output formatting leaves something to be desired, visually speaking.
examples.suggested: עיצוב הפלט הזה מותיר מה לרצות מבחינה ויזואלית.
examples.translation: עיצוב הפלט הזה מניח מה לרצות מבחינה ויזואלית.
examples.why: Calqued idiom with the wrong verb: מניח means 'places/assumes', not 'leaves'. The set phrase in Hebrew is מותיר/משאיר מה לרצות; as written it reads as broken MT.

examples.source: we may define a quantum circuit … the unitary matrix corresponding to this circuit … described by the circuit … the state obtained from the circuit above
examples.suggested: ניתן להגדיר מעגל קוונטי … המטריצה האוניטרית המתאימה למעגל זה … המתואר על ידי המעגל … מהמעגל לעיל
examples.translation: ניתן להגדיר Circuit קוונטי … מטריצת היוניטרי המתאימה ל-Circuit זה … המתואר על ידי ה-Circuit … מה-Circuit לעיל
examples.why: Within-file split: the heading and surrounding prose use מעגלים קוונטיים while four sentences drop back to bare English 'Circuit' inside Hebrew syntax; 'unitary' likewise splits between אוניטריות and the ungrammatical מטריצת היוניטרי.

editor_note: Nothing here would mislead a learner — all figures, dates and claims track the English (50 particles, 10,000 cities, 100,000 nodes, 1.88 mixed precision, Gordon Bell six times, five chapters), and no condition or caveat is inverted or dropped. What a native technical editor would change is word-level: "rather, the future…" becomes "מעתה" ("from now on") instead of "אלא", "practitioner" becomes "כמתרגל" (someone doing drills / a TA) rather than "איש מקצוע", "Large Hadron Collider" is "מאיץ ההדרוניות הגדול" (non-word; should be "הדרונים"), and "diagonalization" is consistently "אלכסון" (the noun "diagonal") where Hebrew math uses "ליכסון". Core quantum terms are otherwise consistent and defensible (סופרפוזיציה, שזירה, מעבדים קוונטיים, הפחתת שגיאות), but "Gate" and "Circuit" are left in capitalised Latin script inside Hebrew prose (lines 71, 84, 110, 112) where Hebrew technical writing uses שער/מעגל קוונטי — glossary leakage rather than a field convention. Residual mechanical slips: an untranslated fragment "ה-IBM-built Oak Ridge Summit" and gender error "זו הייתה עידן" (line 35), a typo "ציון ד-exascale" (line 37), "שני התשתיות" for feminine תשתיות (line 46), and the "launchpad" image flattened to "בסיס שלך לעתיד" (line 136).

examples.source: Quantum computers will not replace classical systems; rather, the future of computational science will increasingly depend on hybrid workflows
examples.suggested: מחשבים קוונטיים לא יחליפו מערכות קלאסיות; אלא, עתיד המדע החישובי יסתמך יותר ויותר על תהליכי עבודה היברידיים
examples.translation: מחשבים קוונטיים לא יחליפו מערכות קלאסיות; מעתה, עתיד המדע החישובי יסתמך יותר ויותר על תהליכי עבודה היברידיים
examples.why: Contrastive 'rather' is rendered as the temporal 'מעתה' ('from now on'). The claim survives, but the logical connective between the two clauses is lost — a Hebrew reader gets a time statement where the English gives a correction.

examples.source: As a practitioner, researcher, or technologist
examples.suggested: כאיש מקצוע, חוקר או טכנולוג
examples.translation: כמתרגל, חוקר, או איש טכנולוגיה
examples.why: 'מתרגל' in Hebrew means someone doing exercises/drills, or a university teaching assistant — not a working professional. Recognisable from context but the wrong noun for 'practitioner'.

examples.source: feeding circuits into the quantum processor / familiarity with quantum gates and circuits / build quantum circuits
examples.suggested: הזנת מעגלים למעבד הקוונטי / היכרות עם שערים ומעגלים קוונטיים / לבניית מעגלים קוונטיים
examples.translation: הזנת Circuit למעבד הקוונטי / הכרות עם Gate ו-Circuit קוונטיים / לבניית Circuit קוונטי
examples.why: Hebrew technical writing uses מעגל קוונטי and שער — these are not terms the field keeps in English. Capitalised Latin singulars embedded mid-sentence (and always singular where English is plural) read as glossary leakage, not convention.

examples.source: This was an era of enormous growth in massively parallel systems… The IBM-built Oak Ridge Summit was the first HPC resource to achieve ExaOPS
examples.suggested: זה היה עידן של צמיחה עצומה… מחשב-העל Oak Ridge Summit, מתוצרת IBM, היה משאב ה-HPC הראשון שהגיע ל-ExaOPS
examples.translation: זו הייתה עידן של צמיחה עצומה במערכות מקביליות מסיביות… ה-IBM-built Oak Ridge Summit היה ה-HPC הראשון שהגיע ל-ExaOPS
examples.why: 'ה-IBM-built' is an untranslated English fragment left inside Hebrew prose; 'זו הייתה עידן' has a gender mismatch (עידן is masculine); and 'resource' is dropped so it reads 'the first HPC' rather than 'the first HPC resource'.

examples.source: Think of this course as your launchpad—the place where you build the mental toolkit and the self-confidence to explore the quantum-classical frontier
examples.suggested: חשוב על הקורס הזה כעל כן השיגור שלך – המקום שבו אתה בונה את ארגז הכלים המנטלי ואת הביטחון העצמי לחקור את הגבול הקוונטי-קלאסי
examples.translation: חשוב על הקורס הזה כבסיס שלך לעתיד – המקום שבו אתה בונה את ארגז הכלים המנטלי ואת הביטחון העצמי לחקור את גבול הקוונטי-קלאסי
examples.why: The launchpad image (which pairs with 'frontier' and closes the lesson) is flattened to the generic 'your basis for the future'; the closing analogy of the lesson is lost. Also 'גבול הקוונטי-קלאסי' should be 'הגבול הקוונטי-קלאסי'.

examples.source: sample-based quantum diagonalization (SQD)
examples.suggested: אלגוריתם ליכסון קוונטי מבוסס-דגימה (SQD)
examples.translation: אלגוריתם אלכסון קוונטי מבוסס-דגימה (SQD)
examples.why: 'אלכסון' is the noun 'diagonal'; the linear-algebra operation 'diagonalization' is 'ליכסון' in Hebrew. Consistently applied across all three occurrences, so the concept stays identifiable, but it is the wrong nominalisation for a named algorithm the course builds on.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — no drift: the error-ordering claim (readout > 2-qubit > 1-qubit), the "least busy Eagle" backend choice, the heavy-hex lattice description and both T1/T2 median exercises all match the English, and the informal "kamu"/"aksesmu" register holds with no deferential slips. The defects are stylistic. (1) Glossary-protected terms are capitalized mid-sentence — "Gate entangling 2-Qubit", "operasi 2-Qubit ... operasi 1-Qubit", "visualisasi Circuit" — which clashes with the correct lowercase used elsewhere in the same file ("Perangkat Eagle memiliki 127 qubit", heading "Properti qubit"), so qubit/gate appear in two casings within one document. (2) Two relative-clause calques read as MT rather than native technical prose: "pasangan yang padanya kamu bisa langsung menerapkan..." (to which) and the sentence-initial "Berikut, kita memilih" for "In the following, we pick". (3) In the appendix, English "visualizers" (the tools) is flattened to "visualisasi" (the act), so "It includes circuit visualizers, state and distribution visualizers, and target visualizer" becomes a list of activities rather than of Qiskit facilities. None of these would give a learner a false belief.

examples.source: Edges indicate pairs to which you can directly apply the 2-qubit entangling gate.
examples.suggested: Edge menunjukkan pasangan qubit yang bisa langsung kamu kenai gate entangling dua-qubit.
examples.translation: Edge menunjukkan pasangan yang padanya kamu bisa langsung menerapkan Gate entangling 2-Qubit.
examples.why: "yang padanya" is a literal calque of English "to which" that no Indonesian technical writer would use; the half-translated compound "Gate entangling 2-Qubit" with mid-sentence capitals compounds the stiffness.

examples.source: the errors of readout tend to be larger than those of the 2-qubit operation, which in turn tend to be larger than the 1-qubit operation
examples.suggested: error readout cenderung lebih besar daripada operasi 2-qubit, yang pada gilirannya cenderung lebih besar daripada operasi 1-qubit
examples.translation: error readout cenderung lebih besar dari operasi 2-Qubit, yang pada gilirannya cenderung lebih besar dari operasi 1-Qubit
examples.why: "Qubit" is capitalized here (and in "Gate", "Circuit" elsewhere) while the same term is correctly lowercase at line 119 ("127 qubit") and in the section heading "Properti qubit" — within-file casing inconsistency, plus "lebih besar dari" should be "daripada" in a comparison.

examples.source: In the following, we pick "ibm_kyoto" , "ibm_kawasaki" or the least busy Eagle machine.
examples.suggested: Pada contoh berikut, kita memilih "ibm_kyoto", "ibm_kawasaki", atau mesin Eagle yang paling senggang.
examples.translation: Berikut, kita memilih "ibm_kyoto", "ibm_kawasaki" atau mesin Eagle yang paling tidak sibuk.
examples.why: Bare sentence-initial "Berikut," is an unidiomatic word-for-word render of "In the following"; a native writer would write "Pada contoh berikut" or "Di bawah ini".

examples.source: It includes circuit visualizers, state and distribution visualizers, and target visualizer.
examples.suggested: Ini mencakup alat visualisasi sirkuit, alat visualisasi state dan distribusi, serta alat visualisasi target.
examples.translation: Ini mencakup visualisasi Circuit, state dan distribusi, serta visualisasi target.
examples.why: English names three concrete tools (visualizers) that Qiskit ships; "visualisasi" names the activity instead, so the learner loses the point that these are distinct facilities they can call — and the following sentence "Kamu sudah menggunakan dua yang pertama" refers back to tools, not activities.

editor_note: The translation is faithful, fluent and reads like a working Indonesian quantum engineer wrote it: core terms are correct and consistent throughout (qubit/gate/circuit/backend/observable/swap kept in English per the field's convention, expectation value → "nilai ekspektasi", quasi-probability distribution → "distribusi kuasiprobabilitas", single-qubit operations → "operasi qubit tunggal", sampling overhead → "overhead sampling"), the informal "kita/kamu" register holds with no bapak/ibu slips, and the load-bearing numbers (two swaps each way, depth reduced by more than half, three CNOTs → $9^3$) all survive. Three small things a native technical editor would still change: "arbitrarily chosen subexperiment" becomes "dipilih secara acak" (= randomly chosen), which quietly implies a random draw where the English just means an arbitrary index (100) picked for illustration; "Backend" and "Primitive" are capitalized mid-sentence ("dijalankan pada Backend", "dengan Sampler Primitive") where the English has them lowercase and the rest of the file writes "backend" lowercase; and "instansi `QPDBasis`" is a calque for "instances" that Indonesian Qiskit prose normally renders as "objek" or "instans". None of these would mislead a learner.

examples.source: Here is an example of an arbitrarily chosen subexperiment generated from the QPD circuit.
examples.suggested: Berikut ini adalah contoh subeksperimen yang dipilih sembarang dari circuit QPD.
examples.translation: Berikut ini adalah contoh subeksperimen yang dipilih secara acak dari circuit QPD.
examples.why: "secara acak" = randomly/at random, implying a stochastic draw. The English "arbitrarily chosen" means the author simply picked index 100 with no particular criterion — deterministic, not random. In a passage that is already about probabilistic subexperiments and sampling, the word "acak" can nudge the learner into thinking the displayed subexperiment was sampled from the quasiprobability distribution.

examples.source: Generate the subexperiments to run on the backend / Execute the target circuits ("subexperiments") with the Sampler primitive.
examples.suggested: ... untuk dijalankan pada backend / ... dengan primitive Sampler.
examples.translation: Buat subeksperimen untuk dijalankan pada Backend / Jalankan circuit target ("subeksperimen") dengan Sampler Primitive.
examples.why: "Backend" and "Primitive" are capitalized mid-sentence as if they were proper nouns or class names, while the same file writes "backend" lowercase elsewhere (line 118, "satu atau lebih backend") and the heading keeps "Qiskit primitives" lowercase. Inconsistent casing of a core domain term within one file.

examples.source: return a list of `QPDBasis` instances / a circuit containing `TwoQubitQPDGate` instances
examples.suggested: mengembalikan daftar objek `QPDBasis` / circuit yang mengandung objek `TwoQubitQPDGate`
examples.translation: mengembalikan daftar instansi `QPDBasis` / circuit yang mengandung instansi `TwoQubitQPDGate`
examples.why: "instansi" is a direct calque of "instance"; in Indonesian it most commonly means "institution/agency" (as in "instansi pemerintah"), so a native reader briefly parses it wrongly. Indonesian technical prose uses "objek" or "instans" for OOP instances — and the same paragraph already uses "objek `TwoQubitQPDGate`" two sentences earlier, so the file is inconsistent with itself.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — I checked the drift-prone passages (the merge_bounds paragraph "passare dai limiti backward ai limiti forward", the Important Note "Il punto in cui passare dai limiti forward a quelli backward dipende dai tassi di rumore appresi", the qubit-6 backward-bound bullet "un errore Z non riesce a commutare, mentre un errore X commuta", and the plateau claim in the locality paragraph) and all match the English; register is consistently informal ("Scopri di più", "fai riferimento", "puoi regolare"). The defects are lexical/consistency ones. First, a glossary leak: the English word "Circuit" (capitalised) survives in six prose spots where the rest of the file says "circuito" — "al layer $l$ nel Circuit", "PEC è spesso limitato a Circuit poco profondi", "a ogni potenziale errore nel Circuit", "dimostrazione con Circuit speculare", "uno o più Circuit di interesse", "ogni possibile errore di rumore nel Circuit". Second, "bound(s)" is split between "limiti" (dominant, used in the headings and the a/b/c workflow list) and untranslated "bounds" (~10 prose occurrences: "i bounds ombreggiati", "bounds banali pari a due", "restringiamo i bounds", "i bounds di rumore previsti"); similarly "antinoise" appears as "anti-rumore", "antinoise", "rumore inverso" and "noise"/"noise learning" is left in English at lines 202 and 275 while elsewhere it is "rumore"/"apprendimento del rumore", and "edge" is "arco" (lines 23, 339) but "bordi spettatori" in Step 4. Third, two real language errors: "il primitivo Executor" / "il primitivo `Executor`" (primitive is feminine in Italian usage — "la primitiva Executor"), and the future-tense typo "traspilaremo" for "traspileremo"; plus the calqued "Per i Clifford gate, vengono spinti verso l'inizio del circuito" (dangling subject; should be "I gate Clifford vengono spinti…").

examples.source: the learned noise rate of error Pauli σ at layer l in the circuit … PEC is often limited to shallow or few-qubit circuits
examples.suggested: … al layer $l$ nel circuito … limitato a circuiti poco profondi o con pochi qubit
examples.translation: il tasso di rumore appreso dell'errore Pauli $\sigma$ al layer $l$ nel Circuit … PEC è spesso limitato a Circuit poco profondi o con pochi qubit
examples.why: Untranslated capitalised "Circuit" leaks into Italian prose in six places while the same paragraph uses "circuito" correctly; the reader sees the same concept under two names in one sentence.

examples.source: You can interpret the behavior of the shaded bounds … the remaining layers to the left are filled entirely with trivial bounds of two
examples.suggested: …il comportamento dei limiti ombreggiati … con limiti banali pari a due
examples.translation: Puoi interpretare il comportamento dei bounds ombreggiati … i layer rimanenti a sinistra vengono riempiti interamente con bounds banali pari a due
examples.why: "bound" is rendered as "limiti" in the headings and workflow list but left as English "bounds" in about ten prose occurrences — within-file inconsistency for the file's central concept.

examples.source: Qiskit IBM Runtime with the Executor primitive … run on a QPU with the `Executor` primitive
examples.suggested: …con la primitiva Executor … eseguiti su una QPU con la primitiva `Executor`
examples.translation: Qiskit IBM Runtime con il primitivo Executor … eseguiti su un QPU con il primitivo `Executor`
examples.why: In Italian Qiskit usage the term is "la primitiva" (feminine); "il primitivo" reads as the adjective "primitive" and is not the conventional domain term.

examples.source: we will transpile our circuit to ISA instructions … For Clifford gates, they are pushed toward the beginning of the circuit.
examples.suggested: traspileremo il nostro circuito in istruzioni ISA … I gate Clifford vengono invece spinti verso l'inizio del circuito.
examples.translation: traspilaremo il nostro circuito in istruzioni ISA … Per i Clifford gate, vengono spinti verso l'inizio del circuito.
examples.why: "traspilaremo" is a malformed future (should be "traspileremo"), and "Per i Clifford gate, vengono spinti" keeps English word order plus a dangling subject — a native technical writer would recast the clause.

examples.source: antinoise (inverse noise) … where antinoise should be injected … for the purpose of noise learning and noise injection
examples.suggested: Usare "anti-rumore" ovunque e "apprendimento del rumore / iniezione del rumore" per noise learning/injection
examples.translation: l'anti-rumore (rumore inverso) … dove … l'antinoise deve essere iniettato … ai fini del noise learning e dell'iniezione di noise
examples.why: The same concept appears as "anti-rumore", "antinoise" and "rumore inverso" (the latter in the Step 3c heading), and "noise"/"noise learning" are left untranslated at lines 202 and 275 although the file elsewhere says "rumore"/"apprendimento del rumore".

editor_note: The translation is faithful, fluent and idiomatic throughout: the conditional clause "purché implementi l'interfaccia BackendV2" correctly renders "as long as it implements", "pronte all'uso" is a natural equivalent of "out-of-the-box", and the caveat "richiede un backend che supporti l'opzione `memory`" is preserved exactly. Terminology is stable and conventional (primitive/primitiva, backend, provider, Estimator/Sampler kept in English, "mitigazione degli errori"), and the informal tu register holds ("Inizia", "Consulta"). The one thing a native technical editor would change is the mid-sentence capitalized "Gate" in "mitigazione degli errori di misura o di Gate" (line 16): Italian does not capitalize this common noun, and the capital reads as a glossary-substitution artifact rather than a deliberate choice — it should be "errori di misura o di gate". Nothing here misleads a learner.

examples.source: it offers no measurement or gate error mitigation implementations "out-of-the-box"
examples.suggested: non offre implementazioni di mitigazione degli errori di misura o di gate "pronte all'uso"
examples.translation: non offre implementazioni di mitigazione degli errori di misura o di Gate "pronte all'uso"
examples.why: "Gate" is capitalized mid-sentence; in Italian technical prose the borrowed noun stays lowercase ("errori di gate"). The capital looks like an automated glossary substitution rather than an editorial choice, and it is the only typographic slip in an otherwise clean file.

editor_note: Nothing here misleads: Sampler/Estimator are not swapped (確率分布 vs 観測量の期待値), the LSb-0 bit-ordering paragraph keeps left/right and most-significant correct, and register is consistently plain です/ます with no keigo. The dominant defect is a pervasive glossary leak: "circuit", "gate", "qubit" and "backend" are left as capitalized English inside Japanese sentences — 量子Circuit を実行する, Circuit と演算子, 測定Gate を追加, 測定したいQubit セット, Backend デバイス — where Japanese quantum docs universally write 量子回路 / ゲート / 量子ビット / バックエンド; capitalization is also unstable (Qubit at L267/288 vs lowercase "qubit 接続性" at L308). Secondary: two calques and a wrong verb — "walk through a Qiskit Patterns workflow" becomes ワークフローを歩んで (L12), while the frontmatter renders the same phrase naturally as 順を追って体験し; and "make sure that it is compatible" becomes 互換性を保護してください (protect compatibility) instead of 確保. Also: the credit-card reassurance drops "or at random after registering" (L19); "operator" splits between 演算子 (L179) and オペレーター (L186); "Qiskit Patterns" splits between Qiskit Patterns (L12) and Qiskit パターン (L171/173/175); and "the set of instructions that the circuit contains" is rendered 命令セット (L308), colliding with 命令セットアーキテクチャ(ISA) two clauses later.

examples.source: you can obtain a probability distribution for a set of qubits you choose to measure … we need to add measurement gates to our circuit … the device's basis gates and qubit connectivity
examples.suggested: 測定したい量子ビットの集合について確率分布を得ることができます … 回路に測定ゲートを追加する必要があります … デバイスの基底ゲートと量子ビット間の結合
examples.translation: 測定したいQubit セットの確率分布を取得することができます … Circuit に測定Gate を追加する必要があります … デバイスの基底Gate と qubit 接続性
examples.why: circuit/gate/qubit/backend are left as capitalized English mid-sentence throughout (量子Circuit, 測定Gate, Qubit セット, Backend デバイス). These are exactly the terms Japanese Qiskit documentation translates (量子回路 / ゲート / 量子ビット / バックエンド); leaving them in English reads as an untranslated glossary leak rather than a convention, and the same word appears as both Qubit (L267, L288) and qubit (L308).

examples.source: In this notebook you will walk through a Qiskit Patterns workflow, and use Qiskit's Sampler primitive.
examples.suggested: このノートブックでは、Qiskit Patterns のワークフローを順を追って進めながら、Qiskit の Sampler プリミティブを使用します。
examples.translation: このノートブックではQiskit Patternsのワークフローを歩んで、Qiskitの[Sampler primitive]を使用します。
examples.why: ワークフローを歩んで is a literal calque of "walk through" — 歩む means to walk/tread a path in life and is never used for stepping through a procedure. The file's own frontmatter description already renders the identical English as 順を追って体験し, so the body is both unnatural and inconsistent with the metadata; "Sampler primitive" is also left in English here while every other occurrence is Sampler プリミティブ.

examples.source: Check that the version of Python you are using in your environment is python>=3.10, to make sure that it is compatible with the latest Qiskit version:
examples.suggested: 環境で使用しているPythonのバージョンがpython>=3.10であることを確認し、最新のQiskitバージョンとの互換性を確保してください：
examples.translation: 使用するPythonのバージョンがpython>=3.10であることを確認して、最新のQiskitバージョンとの互換性を保護してください：
examples.why: 互換性を保護する (protect compatibility) is the wrong verb — 互換性 collocates with 確保する/保つ. 保護 suggests defending something under threat, which a native technical writer would never write here.

examples.source: Your credit card is not charged in this process or at random after registering.
examples.suggested: このプロセスでも、登録後に不定期に請求が発生することもありません。
examples.translation: このプロセスでクレジットカードに請求が発生することはありません。
examples.why: The second half of the reassurance ("or at random after registering") is dropped. The English deliberately covers both the sign-up moment and any later surprise charge; the Japanese only rules out the first, leaving the reader's actual worry — being billed later — unanswered.

examples.source: Optimize the circuits and operators. … *operators* represent the observables to be measured
examples.suggested: Use 演算子 in both places (量子回路と演算子を最適化します … 演算子は測定する観測量を表します)
examples.translation: Circuit と演算子を最適化します。 … *オペレーター* は測定する観測量を表します
examples.why: "operator" is rendered 演算子 in the four-step Qiskit Patterns list and オペレーター seven lines later in the sentence that defines it. The definition sentence is where the learner anchors the term, so the split is most damaging exactly there; 演算子 is the standard rendering. The framework name likewise splits between Qiskit Patterns (L12) and Qiskit パターン (L171/173/175).

examples.source: it is important to optimize the set of instructions that the circuit contains and minimize the overall depth … must conform to a backend device's Instruction Set Architecture (ISA)
examples.suggested: 回路に含まれる命令の集合を最適化し …
examples.translation: Circuit に含まれる命令セットを最適化し、Circuit の全体的な深さ（おおよそ命令数）を最小化することが重要です … Backend デバイスの命令セットアーキテクチャ（ISA）に準拠し
examples.why: "the set of instructions" is rendered 命令セット, the established Japanese term for a hardware instruction set, and 命令セットアーキテクチャ（ISA）appears in the same paragraph. A learner may read the first sentence as being about the ISA rather than about the circuit's own instruction list; 命令の集合 or 命令列 keeps the two ideas distinct.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — I found no semantic drift, no inverted conditions, no dropped caveats, and the sentence-level Korean is genuinely well-written (the LSb-0 bit-ordering paragraph at L268 and the ISA/depth-optimization paragraph at L309 both read naturally and preserve the English reasoning exactly). The defect is a pervasive glossary leak: "circuit" is left as capitalized English "Circuit" 28 times inside Korean prose ("양자 Circuit을 만들 때", "Circuit과 연산자를 최적화합니다", "Circuit에 측정 Gate를 추가해야 합니다") and "gate" as "Gate" 3 times ("측정 Gate", "기저 Gate(basis gate)") — the project's own translation/glossary/ko.json declares preferred="회로"/"게이트" and lists exactly "Circuit"/"Gate" under leaked_en, so these are leaks by the repo's own definition, and 회로/게이트 are the universal Korean domain terms a native quantum engineer would write. "Backend" is likewise left as capitalized English 6 times where 백엔드 is standard. Minor secondary point: "workflow" is rendered 워크플로 at L13 but 워크플로우 at L366. Nothing here misleads a learner (Circuit/Gate/Backend stay recognizable, and lowercase "qubit" is explicitly sanctioned by keep_lowercase), and register (합니다체) matches the ko corpus convention, so this is MINOR rather than FAIL.

examples.source: When creating quantum circuits, you must also consider what type of data you want returned after execution. … so we need to add measurement gates to our circuit.
examples.suggested: 양자 회로를 만들 때, … 회로에 측정 게이트를 추가해야 합니다.
examples.translation: 양자 Circuit을 만들 때, 실행 후 반환될 데이터의 유형도 고려해야 합니다. … Circuit에 측정 Gate를 추가해야 합니다.
examples.why: 'Circuit' (28×) and 'Gate' (3×) are left as capitalized English inside Korean prose. translation/glossary/ko.json sets preferred="회로"/"게이트" and lists "Circuit"/"Gate" explicitly under leaked_en, so these are untranslated leaks; 양자 회로 / 측정 게이트 are what a Korean quantum engineer actually writes.

examples.source: transforms the circuit and observables to match that backend's ISA … must conform to a backend device's Instruction Set Architecture (ISA)
examples.suggested: 해당 백엔드의 ISA에 맞게 회로와 관측 가능량을 변환합니다 … 백엔드 장치의 명령 집합 아키텍처(ISA)를 따라야 하며
examples.translation: 해당 Backend의 ISA에 맞게 Circuit과 관측 가능량을 변환합니다 … Backend 장치의 명령 집합 아키텍처(ISA)를 따라야 하며
examples.why: 'Backend' is kept as capitalized English 6× where 백엔드 is the settled Korean rendering; capitalized Latin nouns mid-sentence read as machine/glossary output rather than native technical writing.

examples.source: you will walk through a Qiskit Patterns workflow … feed these results into another workflow
examples.suggested: pick one form (워크플로) and use it in both places
examples.translation: Qiskit Patterns 워크플로를 따라가며 … 이 결과를 다른 워크플로우에 전달하거나
examples.why: Within-file inconsistency for the same term: 워크플로 at the intro, 워크플로우 in Step 4. Harmless but a native editor would unify it.

editor_note: Prose is genuinely natural Korean technical writing (e.g. "각 스핀은 이웃 스핀과 상호작용하는 동시에 양자 요동을 유발하는 외부 자기장의 영향을 받습니다"), physics is faithful, and no sentence would mislead a learner — but a native editor would fix several term problems. The worst is "unitary evolution operator" rendered as "단일 시간 진화 연산자" in the Overview: 단일 reads as "single", so the unitarity qualifier is silently lost (should be 유니터리 시간 진화 연산자). "circuit" is split within the file between the English glossary form ("Circuit을 구성합니다", "Trotterized Circuit") and 회로 ("Trotter 회로" in two headings), and "observable" is split between 관측값 (which actually means "observed value") in the Overview and 관측량 in the Fire Opal section; "correlators ⟨Z_i Z_j⟩" is flattened to 상관관계 ("correlation") rather than 상관자, and "Qiskit Function" appears once as "Qiskit 함수". Minor drift in the survey blurb ("content offerings" → "콘텐츠 품질", "take a minute" dropped, intensifier 큰 added) and the dropped "to your local environment" in Setup. Register is uniform 합니다체 throughout with no 드리/honorific slips.

examples.source: you use a Trotter decomposition of the unitary evolution operator $e^{-iHt}$, implemented through layers of RX and RZZ gates
examples.suggested: RX 및 RZZ Gate 레이어를 통해 구현된 유니터리 시간 진화 연산자 $e^{-iHt}$의 Trotter 분해를 사용합니다
examples.translation: RX 및 RZZ Gate 레이어를 통해 구현된 단일 시간 진화 연산자 $e^{-iHt}$의 Trotter 분해를 사용합니다
examples.why: 'unitary' is rendered as 단일, which a Korean reader parses as 'single/sole'. The unitarity property — the whole reason e^{-iHt} is decomposable this way — disappears; the standard term is 유니터리.

examples.source: Generate Trotterized circuits on spin graphs / we construct circuits that approximate the time evolution operator

examples.why: 'circuit' alternates between the kept-English 'Circuit' in body prose and 회로 in the section headings within the same file; the same concept is labelled two ways a few lines apart.

examples.source: more reliable estimates of spin observables like $\langle Z_i \rangle$ and correlators $\langle Z_i Z_j \rangle$
examples.suggested: $\langle Z_i \rangle$ 및 상관자 $\langle Z_i Z_j \rangle$와 같은 스핀 관측량(옵저버블)에 대해 더 신뢰할 수 있는 추정치

examples.why: 'observable' becomes 관측값 ('observed value') here but 관측량 later ('파울리-Z 관측량'), and 'correlator' is flattened to 상관관계 ('correlation') — the operator sense is lost in both.

examples.source: Please take a minute to provide feedback on this tutorial. Your insights will help us improve our content offerings and user experience.
examples.suggested: 잠시 시간을 내어 이 튜토리얼에 대한 피드백을 남겨 주세요. 여러분의 의견은 콘텐츠 제공과 사용자 경험을 개선하는 데 도움이 됩니다.

examples.why: 'take a minute' is dropped, 'content offerings' narrows to 콘텐츠 품질 ('content quality'), and the intensifier 큰 strengthens a claim the English does not make.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — no inversions, quantities, bounds ("batas atas"), or caveats are lost, and the VQE/SPSA explanations teach as well as the English ("Penyelesai Nilai Eigen Kuantum Variatif", "dataran tandus", "kecerunan", "transpilasi" are all correct and consistent). Two terminology defects a native editor would fix: (a) "observable" is rendered as the adjectival calque "boleh diperhatikan" in all three step I/O bullets, so "Input: Circuit abstrak, boleh diperhatikan" reads as "abstract circuit, (which is) observable" rather than naming the observable as a second object — the noun "cerapan/kebolehcerapan" or keeping "observable" is needed; (b) "circuit" is split within the file between an untranslated capitalized "Circuit" mid-sentence (lines ~124, 125, 127, 151, 154, 156, and "pustaka Circuit Qiskit" at 43) and the correct Malay "litar" (lines 290, 297) — a glossary-leak artifact. Smaller items: "small deviations" → "penyelewengan kecil" (penyelewengan connotes misconduct; "sisihan" is the technical word); "noise" alternates between "berderau" (43) and "hingar" (165, 290); "diagonalizes it" → "menyelesaikannya secara pepenjuru" ("solves it diagonally") instead of "mempepenjurukannya"; and the register mixes "anda" (18, 46, 307) with "kamu" (20, 26, 293, 295, 310), with a couple of stiff calques ("kamu boleh menjangka untuk memahami", "keputusan yang boleh dihasilkan semula secara boleh dipercayai"). None of this would mislead a learner.

examples.source:
* Input: Abstract circuit, observable
* Output: Target circuit and observable, optimized for the selected QPU

* Output: Litar sasaran dan observable, dioptimumkan untuk QPU yang dipilih

* Input: Circuit abstrak, boleh diperhatikan
* Output: Circuit sasaran dan boleh diperhatikan, dioptimumkan untuk QPU yang dipilih

In a bullet list of step inputs/outputs it reads as a property of the circuit rather than a second object, obscuring that the Hamiltonian/observable is itself transformed by apply_layout.

examples.source: ...an optimization routine for our circuit... / optimizing the circuit parameters / the transpiled circuit depth
