Minor calques remain: "En cambio" used for "Instead" where "En su lugar" is meant (lines 544, 751), "especificaciones de valor de array", and the passive "instanciarse por el usuario".

examples.source: The following gate methods have been removed in favor of more established methods that append the same gates: … Instead, these gates can be applied to a circuit with `QuantumCircuit.append`.
examples.suggested: Los siguientes métodos de puerta han sido eliminados en favor de métodos más consolidados que añaden las mismas puertas: … En su lugar, estas puertas se pueden aplicar a un circuito con `QuantumCircuit.append`.
examples.translation: Los siguientes métodos de Gate han sido eliminados en favor de métodos más consolidados que agregan los mismos gates: … En su lugar, estos gates se pueden aplicar a un Circuit con `QuantumCircuit.append`.
examples.why: "gate" and "circuit" are left in English and capitalized, so "métodos de Gate" reads as if a Gate class owned the methods; the same file translates them correctly as "puertas de circuito" and "circuito" in the pulse and extensions sections.

examples.source: The new V2 primitives are designed to accept vectorized inputs, where single circuits can be grouped with array-valued specifications. That is, one circuit can be executed for arrays of `n` parameter sets…
examples.suggested: …donde un único circuito puede agruparse con especificaciones con valores de array. Es decir, un circuito puede ejecutarse para arrays de `n` conjuntos de parámetros…
examples.translation: Los nuevos primitivos V2 están diseñados para aceptar entradas vectorizadas, donde un único Circuit puede agruparse con especificaciones de valor de array. Es decir, un circuito puede ejecutarse para arrays de `n` conjuntos de parámetros…
examples.why: The same noun appears as English "Circuit" and Spanish "circuito" within two consecutive clauses, and "especificaciones de valor de array" is a word-order calque of "array-valued specifications".

examples.source: the legacy OpenQASM 2 parser … the abstract syntax tree returned by the `ply` parser library
examples.suggested: Pick one: "el analizador (parser) heredado de OpenQASM 2" everywhere, and "analiza tus archivos OpenQASM 2" instead of "parsea".
examples.translation: el parser heredado de OpenQASM 2 … / El módulo heredado del analizador de OpenQASM 2 … devuelto por la biblioteca de análisis `ply`
examples.why: "parser" is rendered as English "parser" in the qiskit.converters section and as "analizador" in the qiskit.qasm section, with the anglicised verb "parsea" in between — a reader may not connect the two sections.

examples.source: Importing from `qiskit.providers.aer` is no longer possible. Instead, import from `qiskit_aer` … Instead, the provider class must be imported from its submodule and instantiated by the user
examples.suggested: En su lugar, importa desde `qiskit_aer` … En su lugar, debes importar la clase del proveedor desde su submódulo e instanciarla tú mismo
examples.translation: Ya no es posible importar desde `qiskit.providers.aer`. En cambio, importa desde `qiskit_aer` … En cambio, la clase del proveedor debe importarse desde su submódulo e instanciarse por el usuario
examples.why: "En cambio" marks contrast ("on the other hand"), not substitution; the file uses the correct "En su lugar" everywhere else. "instanciarse por el usuario" is a calqued agentive passive a Spanish technical writer would recast as an active clause.

editor_note: Faithful, idiomatic and consistently "tu"; core terms are correct and stable (gate→porte / porte X / porte U3, depth→profondeur, parameterized circuits→circuits paramétrés, qubit/cbit and the Sampler/Estimator primitives kept in English), and the load-bearing caveats survive intact — "ne modifie **pas** les circuits sur lesquels elle opère … utilise l'argument `inplace=True`" and the Sampler-requires / Estimator-must-not-contain measurement contrast in "En revanche, les circuits soumis à une primitive Estimator ne doivent pas contenir de mesures".

No semantic drift: every claim, condition and quantity matches the English (including the source's own quirk of mentioning "valeur d'espérance" on a Sampler page, correctly carried over), the "tu" register holds throughout, and core terms are right and consistent ("registre de sortie", "découplage dynamique", "twirling", "la QPU", "valeur d'espérance", "bloc unifié de primitive (PUB)", "le Transpiler" used the same way in §2 and in the Next-steps list). What a native technical editor would still change is surface polish: "requirements" is calqued as "les exigences suivantes" for package version pins (French would say "les versions/dépendances suivantes" or "les prérequis suivants"), "The code on this page" becomes the anglicism "Le code sur cette page" instead of "Le code de cette page", and there is a grammar slip in §2 where the past participle "appelées" is feminine although its antecedent "circuits" is masculine ("appelés"). Also, "gates" is left in English and inflected as French ("gates fractionnaires", ":::note[Gates fractionnaires]") where the established French domain term is "portes (fractionnaires)" — recognizable and defensible if it is a glossary keep-English decision, but it is the one term choice worth confirming.

examples.source: The code on this page was developed using the following requirements.
examples.suggested: Le code de cette page a été développé avec les versions suivantes.
examples.translation: Le code sur cette page a été développé en utilisant les exigences suivantes.
examples.why: Two calques in one sentence: "sur cette page" for "on this page" (French takes "de cette page"), and "exigences" for software "requirements", which in French means demands/requirements in the contractual sense — for pinned package versions a native writer writes "versions", "dépendances" or "prérequis".

examples.source: The circuit and observable need to be transformed to only use instructions supported by the QPU (referred to as *instruction set architecture (ISA)* circuits).
examples.suggested: … (appelés circuits *d'architecture d'ensemble d'instructions (ISA)*).
examples.translation: Le circuit et l'observable doivent être transformés pour n'utiliser que des instructions prises en charge par la QPU (appelées circuits *d'architecture d'ensemble d'instructions (ISA)*).
examples.why: Agreement error: the participle "appelées" is feminine plural but its antecedent is "circuits" (masculine) — it currently reads as if it agreed with "instructions", which would say the instructions are the ISA circuits. Grammar-level only, the meaning is still recoverable, but a native editor fixes it to "appelés".

examples.source: To use the newly supported [fractional gates](/guides/fractional-gates), set `use_fractional_gates=True` …
examples.suggested: Portes fractionnaires / Pour utiliser les portes fractionnaires récemment prises en charge, définis …
examples.translation: :::note[Gates fractionnaires] / Pour utiliser les [gates fractionnaires](/guides/fractional-gates) récemment pris en charge, définis …
examples.why: "gate" is one of the few quantum terms that French does translate — "porte (quantique)" is the standard rendering; keeping the English noun and inflecting it with a French adjective ("gates fractionnaires") reads as a hybrid, and it also drags the participle agreement along ("pris en charge"). Recognizable, so MINOR, but worth aligning with the glossary.

examples.source: Note that Open Plan users cannot submit session jobs.
examples.suggested: Notez… → "Note que les utilisateurs du plan Open ne peuvent pas soumettre de jobs en mode Session."
examples.translation: Remarque que les utilisateurs du plan Open ne peuvent pas soumettre de jobs de Session.
examples.why: "Remarque que" as a sentence-opening imperative is stiff in French technical prose ("Note que" or "À noter :" is what a native writer uses), and the capitalized "jobs de Session" is an awkward genitive for jobs run in session execution mode — the surrounding sentence already established "mode d'exécution … session", so "en mode Session" would keep the link.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — no drift, no inverted conditions, no wrong domain concepts; register is consistently informal plural-imperative (השתמשו / שימו לב / ראו). The main defect is within-file inconsistency on the core term "circuit": it is rendered as Hebrew מעגל in most prose ("תומכת בציור מעגלים", "דיאגרמת המעגל", "אובייקט מעגל") but left as bare English "Circuit" in four places, including two headings ("ציור Circuit קוונטי", "פונקציית ציור Circuit עצמאית") and even inside one sentence that uses both ("לצייר Circuit עם פונקציה עצמאית במקום כמתודה של אובייקט מעגל") — a glossary-leak artifact a Hebrew technical writer would never produce. Secondary: "שלושת הבאקאנד" is missing the plural (should be הבאקאנדים / הרנדרים, and the English here means the three renderers), "אפשרות ה-scale מקנה סקייל לפלט" is a tautological transliteration of "scales the output", and "פותח בשימוש בדרישות הבאות" is a literal calque of "developed using". None of these would mislead a learner.

examples.source: Draw a quantum circuit / Standalone circuit-drawing function / prefer to draw a circuit with a self-contained function instead of as a method of a circuit object
examples.suggested: ציור מעגל קוונטי / פונקציית ציור מעגל עצמאית / לצייר מעגל עם פונקציה עצמאית במקום כמתודה של אובייקט מעגל
examples.translation: ציור Circuit קוונטי / פונקציית ציור Circuit עצמאית / לצייר Circuit עם פונקציה עצמאית במקום כמתודה של אובייקט מעגל
examples.why: The file's own dominant rendering of "circuit" is מעגל (used in the very same sentence at line 235 and throughout §45, §92, §138), but bare English "Circuit" leaks into two headings and two body sentences. The concept stays identifiable, so this is MINOR, but the split is jarring and should be unified on מעגל.

examples.source: The first two options are shared among all three backends.
examples.suggested: שתי האפשרויות הראשונות משותפות לשלושת הרנדרים.
examples.translation: שתי האפשרויות הראשונות משותפות לכל שלושת הבאקאנד.
examples.why: Two problems: the noun is not pluralized (שלושת הבאקאנד instead of הבאקאנדים), which is ungrammatical after שלושת; and "backends" here means the three output renderers (text/mpl/latex), not Qiskit backends — leaving it as the transliterated hardware term בַּאקאנד invites the wrong association, while the rest of the file already says רנדר.

examples.source: The `scale` option scales the output of the `mpl` and `latex` renderers.
examples.suggested: אפשרות ה-`scale` משנה את קנה המידה של הפלט ברנדרי `mpl` ו-`latex`.
examples.translation: אפשרות ה-`scale` מקנה סקייל לפלט של רנדרי `mpl` ו-`latex`.
examples.why: "מקנה סקייל" is a circular transliteration that explains the option by repeating its English name; Hebrew already has קנה מידה, and the file itself uses בקנה מידה גדול at line 114. A native technical writer would not write מקנה סקייל.

examples.source: The code on this page was developed using the following requirements.
examples.suggested: הקוד בעמוד זה פותח עם הדרישות הבאות.
examples.translation: הקוד בעמוד זה פותח בשימוש בדרישות הבאות.
examples.why: "בשימוש ב..." is a word-for-word calque of English "using"; idiomatic Hebrew uses עם or תוך שימוש ב-. Grammatical but reads as machine output.

examples.source: but when running outside of Jupyter, images will not display automatically
examples.suggested: אך כאשר מריצים את הקוד מחוץ ל-Jupyter, התמונות לא יוצגו אוטומטית
examples.translation: אך כאשר רצים מחוץ ל-Jupyter, תמונות לא יוצגו אוטומטית
examples.why: כאשר רצים reads as "when [people] run/jog" — the intransitive verb loses the object; and the indefinite תמונות should be definite התמונות here. Small fluency slip, meaning still recoverable.

editor_note: Meaning is broadly faithful and the domain terms are right and consistent (מסווג, אנסמבל, לומדים, רגולריזציה, מסווג "משופר קוונטית" for quantum-enhanced, Qubits/Backend/hyperparameters kept in Latin script throughout), so nothing teaches a false concept. Three concrete defects a native editor would fix: (a) in step 4 of "לפתרון בעיית סיווג גנרית", "the number and types of learners" is compressed to "מספר סוגי הלומדים" ("the number of learner types"), collapsing two hyperparameters (`num_learners`, `learners_types`) into one non-existent one; (b) a double-definite smikhut error, "בגלל הגבול ההחלטה הלא-לינארי שלה" — must be "בגלל גבול ההחלטה הלא-לינארי שלה"; (c) the changelog renders "Standardized error handling" as "תקנון טיפול בשגיאות", where תקנון means "bylaws/statute", not standardization (סטנדרטיזציה/האחדת הטיפול בשגיאות). The rest is light translationese: "עבד מראש את סט הנתונים" for "preprocess", "דיוקים גבוהים" as a literal plural of "accuracies", a dangling "משפר את הגמישות" participle, and "ראה ב-[Leclerc...]" for "Review".

examples.source: which accepts hyperparameters such as the number and types of learners, the regularization (lambda value)
examples.suggested: המקבלת hyperparameters כגון מספר הלומדים וסוגיהם, הרגולריזציה (ערך lambda)
examples.translation: המקבלת hyperparameters כגון מספר סוגי הלומדים, הרגולריזציה (ערך lambda)
examples.why: The English names two distinct hyperparameters (how many learners, and of which types — `num_learners` and `learners_types` in the code below). The Hebrew reads "the number of learner types", a single parameter that does not exist in the API; the reader loses `num_learners`.

examples.source: a notoriously challenging problem due to its nonlinear decision boundary
examples.suggested: בעיה ידועה לשמצה בגלל גבול ההחלטה הלא-לינארי שלה
examples.translation: בעיה ידועה לשמצה בגלל הגבול ההחלטה הלא-לינארי שלה
examples.why: Ungrammatical double definite article in a construct chain (הגבול ההחלטה). A Hebrew technical writer would never produce this; the head noun of a smikhut takes no ה-.

examples.source: Standardized error handling
examples.suggested: האחדת הטיפול בשגיאות / סטנדרטיזציה של הטיפול בשגיאות
examples.translation: תקנון טיפול בשגיאות
examples.why: תקנון means "bylaws/regulations", not "standardization". The changelog entry reads as "error-handling bylaws" — recognizable from context but plainly the wrong word.

examples.source: Preprocess the dataset ... enhancing flexibility and overall performance
examples.suggested: בצע עיבוד מקדים של סט הנתונים ... ניתן להרחיב את האנסמבל באופן דינמי ובכך לשפר את הגמישות והביצועים הכוללים
examples.translation: עבד מראש את סט הנתונים ... ניתן להרחיב את האנסמבל באופן דינמי, משפר את הגמישות והביצועים הכוללים
examples.why: Two English-syntax calques: "עבד מראש" is a word-for-word rendering of "preprocess" instead of the standard עיבוד מקדים, and the bare participle "משפר" copies the English -ing clause, leaving a dangling modifier Hebrew does not allow.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — no inverted conditions, swapped quantities, or dropped caveats — and the informal "kamu" register holds consistently ("Kalau kamu ingin mempelajari algoritma ini lebih dalam", "Jika beban kerjamu gagal"). The main defect is terminology: "quantum circuit" is rendered as "Circuit kuantum" with a stray capital C mid-sentence in four paragraphs (Deskripsi section: "parameter Circuit kuantum", "tiga opsi Circuit kuantum", "Circuit kemudian dieksekusi", "Circuit kuantum tidak perlu memperkirakan"), then switches to the correct "sirkuit kuantum" in the very last paragraph of the same section — a visible glossary leak plus within-file split. Second, "sparsity" is rendered "kelangkaan" (economic scarcity), where an Indonesian technical writer would write "sifat jarang"/"kejarangan" or keep "sparsity"; and "the classical generation of additional configurations" becomes "generasi klasik konfigurasi tambahan", where "generasi" carries the "generation = cohort" sense rather than the process sense ("pembangkitan"). Third, "intractable" is softened to "tidak praktis" (impractical) rather than computationally infeasible. None of these would make a learner form a false belief, but each is something a native technical editor would change.

examples.source: The optimization loop focuses on adjusting a quantum circuit's parameters ... HI-VQE offers three quantum circuit options ... the quantum circuit does not need to approximate the full ground state ... the number of shots taken for each quantum circuit
examples.suggested: sirkuit kuantum (lowercase, everywhere)
examples.translation: penyesuaian parameter Circuit kuantum ... tiga opsi Circuit kuantum ... Circuit kuantum tidak perlu memperkirakan ... jumlah shot yang diambil untuk setiap sirkuit kuantum
examples.why: Glossary leak: the English head noun is kept and capitalized mid-sentence ('Circuit kuantum'), which no Indonesian technical writer would produce, and the file then contradicts itself by using the correct 'sirkuit kuantum' in the final paragraph of the same section. Recognizable, so not misleading, but an inconsistent and visibly machine-shaped rendering.

examples.source: Selected configuration interaction (SCI) methods exploit this sparsity to reduce computational costs
examples.suggested: memanfaatkan sifat jarang (sparsity) ini
examples.translation: Metode selected configuration interaction (SCI) memanfaatkan kelangkaan ini untuk mengurangi biaya komputasi
examples.why: 'Kelangkaan' is scarcity in the everyday/economic sense, not the linear-algebra property that most amplitudes are negligible. The intended concept is still inferable from the preceding sentence, so it is imperfect rather than false, but it is not the conventional domain rendering.

examples.source: control the subspace size or enable the classical generation of additional configurations
examples.suggested: mengaktifkan pembangkitan konfigurasi tambahan secara klasik
examples.translation: mengontrol ukuran subspace atau mengaktifkan generasi klasik konfigurasi tambahan
examples.why: 'Generasi' in Indonesian primarily means a generation/cohort of people; used for the process of producing configurations it is a calque of English 'generation', and the stacked noun chain 'generasi klasik konfigurasi tambahan' is hard to parse. The corresponding verb elsewhere in the file is correctly 'menghasilkan', so this spot also reads inconsistently.

examples.source: but this becomes intractable for larger systems since the number of configurations grows exponentially with system size
examples.suggested: tetapi ini menjadi tidak terselesaikan secara komputasional (intractable) untuk sistem yang lebih besar
examples.translation: tetapi ini menjadi tidak praktis untuk sistem yang lebih besar karena jumlah konfigurasi bertumbuh secara eksponensial seiring ukuran sistem
examples.why: 'Tidak praktis' means merely inconvenient/impractical, while 'intractable' is the stronger claim that the computation is infeasible in principle at scale — the exact motivation for the whole method. A mild softening of the claim; the following 'exponentially' clause keeps the learner on track, so it does not mislead outright.

editor_note: No passage misleads a learner: the technical content (exascale/exaflops, factorial vs exponential scaling, QCSC three-tier hardware stack, SQD, "quantum does not eliminate those limits but can sometimes bypass them") is rendered faithfully, and the informal "kamu" register holds throughout with no deferential bapak/ibu slips. The recurring native-speaker defect is the author-"we": "kita mengantisipasi", "kita mengharapkan dua jenis utama peserta", "kita memberikan rekomendasi persiapan", "Kita menyarankan agar peserta...", "Misi kita jelas namun ambisius" all use inclusive kita (we-including-the-reader) where Indonesian requires exclusive kami — as written, the learner is grammatically among the people giving themselves the recommendations. Second, the glossary keeps "Circuit" and "Gate" capitalized in English mid-sentence ("memasukkan Circuit ke prosesor kuantum", "Gate dan Circuit kuantum", "Jalankan Circuit pertamamu") — consistent, so not misleading, but a native technical writer would write sirkuit/gerbang or at least lowercase them. Third, small calques and one untranslated fragment survive: the English idiom "just another HPC resource" becomes the non-idiom "bukan 'sekadar lagi' sumber daya HPC", "The IBM-built Oak Ridge Summit" is left as "IBM-built Oak Ridge Summit", and "orders of magnitude longer than the current age of our Sun" flattens to plain "jauh lebih lama".

examples.source: we anticipate a near future… we expect two main types of learners… we provide preparation recommendations for both groups below… We recommend that participants…
examples.suggested: kami mengantisipasi… kami mengharapkan dua jenis utama peserta… kami memberikan rekomendasi persiapan… Kami menyarankan agar peserta… (and "Misi kami jelas namun ambisius" at line 18)
examples.translation: kita mengantisipasi masa depan dekat… kita mengharapkan dua jenis utama peserta… kita memberikan rekomendasi persiapan untuk kedua kelompok di bawah ini… Kita menyarankan agar peserta…
examples.why: Indonesian distinguishes inclusive kita (we = author + reader) from exclusive kami (we = the course authors). Here the subject is the course team speaking about the learner, so kita is pragmatically wrong: it reads as though the reader is also among those expecting learners and issuing the recommendations. Note lines 14/16 ("pemahaman ilmiah kita", "Kini kita punya") are genuinely inclusive and correctly use kita — only the author-voice sentences need changing.

examples.source: they are not "just another" HPC resources that can be controlled and used in the same way as CPUs, GPUs, etc.
examples.suggested: komputer kuantum bukan sekadar "satu lagi" sumber daya HPC yang bisa dikendalikan dan dipakai persis seperti CPU, GPU, dan sebagainya.
examples.translation: mereka bukan "sekadar lagi" sumber daya HPC yang dapat dikontrol dan digunakan dengan cara yang sama seperti CPU, GPU, dan sebagainya.
examples.why: "sekadar lagi" is a word-for-word calque of "just another" that is not an Indonesian construction — the quoted phrase lands as broken syntax rather than the dismissive idiom the English intends. The same paragraph also opens with a doubled calque, "Ada beberapa cara di mana … dengan cara-cara yang penting bagi kursus ini", repeating cara twice for English "ways in which … in ways that".

examples.source: feeding circuits into the quantum processor / quantum circuit generation / familiarity with quantum gates and circuits / build quantum circuits / Run your first circuit
examples.suggested: sirkuit kuantum / gerbang (gate) dan sirkuit kuantum — or at minimum lowercase "circuit"/"gate" if the keep-English convention is deliberate
examples.translation: memasukkan Circuit ke prosesor kuantum / pembuatan Circuit kuantum / keakraban dengan Gate dan Circuit kuantum / membangun Circuit kuantum / Jalankan Circuit pertamamu
examples.why: The rendering is consistent so the concept stays identifiable, but capitalized bare English nouns inside Indonesian sentences read as untranslated glossary tokens rather than a deliberate keep-English convention; "sirkuit kuantum" and "gerbang kuantum" are the established Indonesian domain terms and the rest of the file otherwise localizes freely (superposisi, prosesor kuantum, mitigasi kesalahan).

examples.source: the calculation would take orders of magnitude longer than the current age of our Sun
examples.suggested: perhitungan tersebut akan memakan waktu berorde-orde besaran lebih lama daripada usia Matahari kita saat ini
examples.translation: perhitungan tersebut akan memakan waktu jauh lebih lama dari usia Matahari kita saat ini
examples.why: "orders of magnitude" is a quantitative claim central to the section's argument about exponential blow-up; "jauh lebih lama" ("much longer") flattens it to a vague comparative and loses the pedagogical punch the paragraph is building toward. Not misleading, but the emphasis is measurably weaker than the English.

examples.source: The IBM-built Oak Ridge Summit was the first HPC resource to achieve ExaOPS
examples.suggested: Oak Ridge Summit buatan IBM adalah sumber daya HPC pertama yang mencapai ExaOPS
examples.translation: IBM-built Oak Ridge Summit adalah sumber daya HPC pertama yang mencapai ExaOPS
examples.why: The English compound modifier "IBM-built" is left untranslated at the head of an Indonesian sentence — a straight leak, not a proper-noun retention (Oak Ridge Summit is the name; IBM-built is a description).

examples.source: having some prior exposure will make the material more accessible … some exposure to sampling-based algorithms
examples.suggested: pengetahuan awal akan membuat materi lebih mudah dipahami … sedikit pengenalan/pengalaman dengan algoritma berbasis sampling
examples.translation: memiliki pengetahuan awal akan membuat materi lebih mudah diakses … beberapa eksposur terhadap algoritma berbasis sampling
examples.why: "lebih mudah diakses" reads as physical/technical access (accessible = reachable) rather than "easier to follow", which is the pedagogical sense here; and "eksposur" is a raw calque of "exposure" that Indonesian technical prose uses for radiation or media exposure, not prior acquaintance with a topic. Both blunt the reassuring, on-ramp tone of the prerequisites section.

editor_note: No misleading content: every numeric fact, condition and caveat survives intact (0.0 = massima approssimazione / 1.0 = nessuna approssimazione, "al massimo tre gate CX", "meno errori dall'hardware ma più errori dall'approssimazione", the swap-permutation caveat in "Layout iniziale"), terminology is correct and consistent (qubit/qubit virtuali/fisici, gate, transpiler + transpilazione, backend, sintesi unitaria, pass, fase), and the informal "tu" register holds throughout ("Puoi usare", "Nota che", "Consulta", "esegui"). Two polish-only spots a native technical editor would still touch: in the opening of "Grado di approssimazione", "specificare quanto vuoi che il circuito risultante corrisponda al circuito desiderato" drops the "closely" of the English — bare "quanto ... corrisponda" reads underspecified where "quanto fedelmente" is the idiomatic rendering; and "Valori più bassi scambiano l'accuratezza dell'output con una maggiore facilità di esecuzione" is a close calque of "trade X for Y" that an Italian writer would phrase as "sacrificano l'accuratezza dell'output a favore di una maggiore facilità di esecuzione". Neither changes the meaning; both are fluency touch-ups.

examples.source: You can use the approximation degree to specify how closely you want the resultant circuit to match the desired (input) circuit.
examples.suggested: Puoi usare il grado di approssimazione per specificare quanto fedelmente vuoi che il circuito risultante corrisponda al circuito desiderato (di input).
examples.translation: Puoi usare il grado di approssimazione per specificare quanto vuoi che il circuito risultante corrisponda al circuito desiderato (di input).
examples.why: "how closely" is the pedagogically load-bearing word — it tells the learner the parameter is a fidelity dial, not an on/off match. Bare "quanto ... corrisponda" flattens that to a vague quantity; "quanto fedelmente" restores the intuition.

examples.source: Smaller values trade output accuracy for ease of execution (that is, fewer gates).
examples.suggested: Valori più bassi sacrificano l'accuratezza dell'output a favore di una maggiore facilità di esecuzione (cioè, meno gate).
examples.translation: Valori più bassi scambiano l'accuratezza dell'output con una maggiore facilità di esecuzione (cioè, meno gate).
examples.why: "scambiare A con B" is a word-for-word mapping of the English "trade X for Y" and reads translated; Italian technical prose expresses this trade-off with "sacrificare ... a favore di" (or "a scapito di", already used correctly later in the same section).

editor_note: No semantic drift: the precedence list (PUB → keyword `precision` → twirling product → `default_shots` → `default_precision`), the "il job fallisce se `twirling` è abilitato e il prodotto ... è minore degli shot necessari" caveat, and "minore è la precision, più tempo QPU è necessario" all track the English exactly, and the "tu" register holds throughout ("Puoi impostare", "Consulta", "Decidi"). What a native editor would change is terminological/stylistic polish: "layer noise learning" is rendered "l'apprendimento del rumore a strati" ("layered/stratified noise") instead of the conventional "rumore dei layer/degli strati del circuito"; "List of directed two-qubit interactions" carries a leftover double gloss "interazioni orientate (dirette)"; "Per vedere le versioni di opzioni precedenti" is a word-order calque of "older option versions" (natural: "le versioni precedenti delle opzioni"); and the accordion title "Versioni dei package" leaves "package" in English where "pacchetti" is the standard Italian, next to the impersonal "Si raccomanda di usare" in an otherwise tu-form file. None of these would mislead a learner.

examples.source: Options for learning layer noise.
examples.suggested: Opzioni per l'apprendimento del rumore dei layer (del circuito).
examples.translation: Opzioni per l'apprendimento del rumore a strati.
examples.why: "a strati" reads as "layered/stratified noise", a property of the noise, rather than "the noise of a circuit layer", which is what layer noise learning actually characterizes. Recognizable but imprecise.

examples.source: **Choices**: List of directed two-qubit interactions
examples.translation: **Scelte**: Lista di interazioni orientate (dirette) a due qubit
examples.why: The parenthetical "(dirette)" is a leftover second rendering of the same English word; a native editor would keep one term ("orientate") and delete the gloss.

examples.source: To see older option versions, visit the `qiskit-ibm-runtime` API reference
examples.suggested: Per vedere le versioni precedenti delle opzioni, visita ...
examples.translation: Per vedere le versioni di opzioni precedenti, visita il riferimento API di `qiskit-ibm-runtime`
examples.why: Calqued noun-stacking from "older option versions"; the Italian word order is stiff and momentarily ambiguous about what "precedenti" modifies.

examples.source: Package versions / We recommend using these versions or newer.
examples.suggested: Versioni dei pacchetti / Ti consigliamo di usare queste versioni o più recenti.
examples.translation: Versioni dei package / Si raccomanda di usare queste versioni o versioni più recenti.
examples.why: "package" is left in English where "pacchetti" is the standard Italian term, and the impersonal "Si raccomanda" sits oddly in a file that otherwise addresses the reader with "tu" ("Puoi", "Consulta", "Decidi").

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — no inverted conditions, swapped quantities or dropped caveats; the GHZ/noise, T₁-decay, Toffoli-decomposition and readout-error explanations all teach as clearly as the English, and register is correctly plain desu/masu with no keigo. The defects are surface-level. (1) The physicist's name is misspelled "DiVincento" in four places (frontmatter description, 「物理学者David DiVincentoは」 in the intro, 「DiVincentoの量子計算のための5つの基準」, and the flying-qubit parenthetical) while the rest of the file correctly says 「DiVincenzo基準」 — the same person spelled two ways in one document. (2) Several core terms split within the file: basis gates are 「ベースGate」 once (「典型的なIBM BackendのベースGate」) but 「基底Gate」 everywhere else; "gate" alternates between the glossary form `Gate` and 「ゲート」 (「ゲート操作時間」, 「2Qubitエンタングリングゲート」); T₂ is 「脱位相」 in the noise-model paragraph but 「位相緩和時間」 in Criterion 3. (3) Glossary substitution left unnatural interpuncts a Japanese engineer would never write — 「Gate・エラー」, 「IBM Quantum・デバイス」, 「IBM Quantum・コンピューター」 — plus a 「なぜなら〜からです」 calque and a dangling 「〜知られており（…）。」 clause. None of this would give a learner a false belief, but a native technical editor would fix all of it.

examples.source: Physicist David DiVincenzo outlined five key requirements … (DiVincenzo also described two criteria for quantum communication …)
examples.suggested: 物理学者David DiVincenzoは…／**DiVincenzoの量子計算のための5つの基準**：／*（DiVincenzoは量子通信のための…）*
examples.translation: 物理学者David DiVincentoは、量子コンピュータのあらゆる物理実装に必要な5つの主要な要件と…／**DiVincentoの量子計算のための5つの基準**：／*（DiVincentoは量子通信のための2つの基準も説明しています…）*
examples.why: Proper noun misspelled as 'DiVincento' in four places while the criteria themselves are consistently 「DiVincenzo基準」 — the same person named two ways in one file. Recognizable, so MINOR, but a learner searching the name would be misdirected.

examples.source: gate errors, finite gate times … / real IBM Quantum devices / real IBM Quantum computer
examples.suggested: Gateエラー、有限のGate時間 … ／実際のIBM Quantumデバイス／実際のIBM Quantumコンピューター
examples.translation: Gate・エラー、有限のGate時間 … ／実際のIBM Quantum・デバイス／実際のIBM Quantum・コンピューター
examples.why: The 「・」 inserted between an English term and its Japanese head noun is a term-substitution artifact, not Japanese punctuation; a native technical writer joins them directly. Note the file itself writes 「IBM Quantum コンピュータ」 without the dot in the Criterion-5 device paragraph, so it is also inconsistent.

examples.source: First, let's see what the basis gates are for a typical IBM backend. … For instance, ibmq_brisbane's basis gates:
examples.suggested: まず、典型的なIBM Backendの基底Gateを確認しましょう。…たとえば、ibmq_brisbaneの基底Gateは以下の通りです。
examples.translation: まず、典型的なIBM BackendのベースGateを確認しましょう。…たとえば、ibmq_brisbaneの基底Gateは以下の通りです。
examples.why: 'Basis gates' is rendered 「ベースGate」 in one sentence and 「基底Gate」 in the very next one (and in Exercise 4, the transpile paragraph and the summary). 「基底Gate」 is the correct convention; 「ベースGate」 should not appear at all.

examples.source: Continuous re-initialization (for quantum error correction) is an active research topic because doing it quickly is challenging.
examples.suggested: （量子エラー訂正のための）継続的な再初期化は、迅速に行うことが難しいため、活発な研究テーマです。
examples.translation: （量子エラー訂正のための）継続的な再初期化は活発な研究テーマです。なぜなら、それを迅速に行うことが難しいからです。
examples.why: English 'because'-clause word order calqued into a separate 「なぜなら〜からです」 sentence — grammatical but reads as machine output; Japanese technical prose subordinates the reason with 「〜ため」 inside the sentence.

examples.source: The IBM devices, for example, have a set of native operations like arbitrary single-qubit rotations and CNOTs between certain qubits, which together are universal.
examples.suggested: たとえばIBMデバイスには、任意の1Qubit回転と、特定のQubit間のCNOTといったネイティブ操作のセットがあり、これらを合わせると普遍的になります。
examples.translation: たとえばIBMデバイスには、特定のQubit間の任意の1Qubit回転とCNOTなど、普遍的なネイティブ操作のセットがあります。
examples.why: 「特定のQubit間の」 modifies 'CNOT' in the English but is fronted so it appears to scope over the single-qubit rotations too; and 'which together are universal' is flattened into 「普遍的なネイティブ操作のセット」, which reads as each operation being universal rather than the set collectively.

examples.source: This set is known to be universal for quantum computing (essentially single-qubit rotations plus an entangling two-qubit gate form a universal set).
examples.suggested: このセットは量子コンピューティングにとって普遍的であることが知られています（基本的に1Qubit回転と2Qubitエンタングリング Gate の組み合わせが普遍集合を形成します）。
examples.translation: このセットは量子コンピューティングにとって普遍的であることが知られており（基本的に1Qubit回転と2Qubitエンタングリングゲートの組み合わせが普遍集合を形成します）。
examples.why: The conjunctive 「〜知られており」 is left dangling: the sentence ends on a parenthetical with no main predicate. Also 「ゲート」 here vs the file-wide `Gate` convention (compare 「基底Gate」 two sentences earlier).

editor_note: The mathematical argument is faithful throughout — the x²≡1, x≢±1 derivation, the order/period equivalence, the |1⟩-as-superposition-of-eigenstates workaround, and the "toy example" caveat about k≥2 powers all land correctly, and 위수/서로소/고유 상태/유니터리/중첩 are the right conventional terms used consistently. What a native technical editor would change is the English-token layer: "Circuit", "Qubit", "Gate", "Backend" are left in capitalized English inside Korean sentences ("양자 Circuit으로 매핑하기", "SWAP Gate", "먼저 Backend를 불러와야 합니다") where 회로/큐비트/게이트/백엔드 are the standard renderings, and the capitalization is internally inconsistent ("제어 Qubit의 수(위 그림에서 상단 $m$개 qubit)"; "Hadamard 게이트" vs "SWAP Gate" in the same file). QPE is likewise split between English "Quantum Phase Estimation" (lines ~235, 249, 251) and "양자 위상 추정" (lines ~533, 810, 817). Two small content slips: both image alt texts describe a^k mod N as "N으로 나눈 값" (the value divided by N) rather than 나눈 나머지, and the closing line adds a superlative not in the English ("가장 흥미로운 시대" for "an exciting time").

examples.source: 1. Mapping your problem to a quantum circuit / First we need to load the backend.
examples.suggested: 1. 문제를 양자 회로로 매핑하기 … 먼저 백엔드를 불러와야 합니다.
examples.translation: 1. 문제를 양자 Circuit으로 매핑하기 … 먼저 Backend를 불러와야 합니다.
examples.why: circuit/backend/gate/qubit are left as capitalized English tokens inside Korean prose. A Korean quantum engineer writes 양자 회로, 백엔드, 게이트, 큐비트; the mixed-script forms read as untranslated glossary leakage, and the file is inconsistent with itself ("Hadamard 게이트" vs "SWAP Gate", "Qubit" vs "qubit" in the same sentence at line 255).

examples.source: Value of a to the power of k modulo N versus the power k, where a=2 and N=15.
examples.suggested: a=2, N=15일 때 거듭제곱 k에 따른 a^k를 N으로 나눈 나머지의 그래프.
examples.translation: a=2, N=15일 때 거듭제곱 k에 따른 a의 k 거듭제곱을 N으로 나눈 값의 그래프.
examples.why: "N으로 나눈 값" means the quotient a^k/N, not the modular residue. The plotted quantity is a^k mod N; the same alt text later says "a^k modulo N", so it contradicts itself. Low visibility (alt text only), hence minor.

examples.source: we just have to make use of Quantum Phase Estimation … the quantum phase estimation algorithm
examples.suggested: pick one: 양자 위상 추정(QPE) throughout, with the English name given once on first mention
examples.translation: Quantum Phase Estimation을 활용하여 … 양자 위상 추정 알고리즘을 실행하려면
examples.why: The same core subroutine is rendered as English "Quantum Phase Estimation" in some paragraphs and "양자 위상 추정" in others (and "Quantum Fourier Transform" in English at line 249 while the intro at line 44 uses "양자 푸리에 변환"). Recognizable, but a learner tracking one concept sees two labels.

examples.source: Shor's algorithm for factoring large numbers … a large, fault-tolerant quantum computer
examples.suggested: 큰 수를 인수분해하는 알고리즘 … 대규모 내결함성 양자 컴퓨터
examples.translation: 대형 수 인수분해 알고리즘 … 대형 내결함성 양자 컴퓨터
examples.why: "대형 수" is not idiomatic Korean for a large number, and the file itself uses the natural "큰 수" two paragraphs later (lines 42, 62). "대형 … 양자 컴퓨터" should be 대규모.

examples.source: It's an exciting time to be learning about quantum computing!
examples.suggested: 양자 컴퓨팅을 배우기에 정말 흥미로운 시기입니다!
examples.translation: 지금이야말로 양자 컴퓨팅을 배우기 가장 흥미로운 시대입니다!
examples.why: Adds a superlative ("가장", the most exciting era) that the English does not claim — a mild strengthening of the closing pitch. Not misleading, but an editor would pull it back.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — no inverted conditions, no swapped quantities, and the tricky iteration-count narrative (2회 최적 → 3회 약간 감소 → 4회 가장 낮은 확률) tracks the English exactly, including the "정답을 얻을 확률이 100%가 아닌 것은 Grover 탐색에서 일반적인 현상입니다" caveat; the EN's own "네 가지 주요 구성 요소" vs. three listed items is a faithful copy of a source bug, not a translation error. The real problem is terminology treatment: core terms are left as capitalized Latin words inside Korean prose — "양자 Circuit을 실행하기 위한 환경", "n-Qubit 레지스터의 각 Qubit에 Hadamard Gate를 적용", "네이티브 기저 Gate", "Qubit의 순서에 주의" — whereas Korean quantum writing invariably uses 양자 회로 / 큐비트 / 게이트, and the same file *does* Koreanize neighbouring terms (레지스터, 시뮬레이터, 디바이스, 트랜스파일, 확산 연산자, 진폭 증폭), so the treatment is inconsistent within the file as well as unidiomatic. Two smaller items: line 352 adds a gloss not in the English ("즉 찾고자 하는 정답 상태입니다" — correct, but an insertion), and the course title renders as the stiff calque "양자 컴퓨팅의 유틸리티로 가는 길". Register is consistently 합니다체/해요체 with no 하십시오체 or 드리- slips.

examples.source: This is achieved by applying a Hadamard gate to each qubit in an n-qubit register
examples.suggested: 이는 n-큐비트 레지스터의 각 큐비트에 아다마르 게이트를 적용함으로써 이루어지며
examples.translation: 이는 n-Qubit 레지스터의 각 Qubit에 Hadamard Gate를 적용함으로써 달성되며
examples.why: Korean quantum documentation writes 큐비트 / 게이트 in Hangul; leaving capitalized 'Qubit'/'Gate' embedded in Korean prose reads as glossary substitution, not as something a Korean engineer wrote — and the same sentence already Koreanizes 레지스터, so the treatment is internally inconsistent.

examples.source: set up the environment for running the quantum circuit / Executing the circuit / converted to a circuit using the native basis gates
examples.suggested: 양자 회로를 실행하기 위한 환경을 설정하고 … 3단계: 회로 실행 … 해당 디바이스의 네이티브 기저 게이트를 사용하는 회로로 변환됩니다
examples.translation: 양자 Circuit을 실행하기 위한 환경을 설정하고 … 3단계: Circuit 실행 … 해당 디바이스의 네이티브 기저 Gate를 사용하는 Circuit으로 변환됩니다
examples.why: 'circuit' is universally 회로 in Korean; the hybrid '네이티브 기저 Gate' (Korean 기저 + Latin Gate) is especially jarring. Recognizable, so not misleading, but a native technical editor would change every instance.

examples.source: This time, $|111\rangle$ is the "good" state.
examples.suggested: 이번에는 $|111\rangle$이 "좋은(good)" 상태입니다.
examples.translation: 이번에는 $|111\rangle$이 "좋은(good)" 상태, 즉 찾고자 하는 정답 상태입니다.
examples.why: The clause '즉 찾고자 하는 정답 상태입니다' is an insertion with no counterpart in the English. It is factually correct and pedagogically harmless, but it is added content and should either be dropped or matched across the file's other terse notes.

examples.source: This notebook is the fourth in a series of lectures on the Path to Utility in Quantum Computing.
examples.suggested: 이 노트북은 '양자 컴퓨팅 유틸리티로 가는 길(Path to Utility in Quantum Computing)' 강의 시리즈의 네 번째입니다.
examples.translation: 이 노트북은 양자 컴퓨팅의 유틸리티로 가는 길에 관한 강의 시리즈의 네 번째입니다.
examples.why: '유틸리티로 가는 길에 관한' is a word-for-word calque of an English course title used as a relative clause; a Korean writer would set the title off as a quoted proper name rather than embed it as descriptive prose.

editor_note: No semantic drift: every heading and the closing sentence track the English faithfully (cut counts, the 4-qubit-per-subcircuit constraint, "satu potongan wayar dan memotong satu `CRZGate`", "Langkah 3 dan 4 ... seperti dalam tutorial sebelumnya" all match), and "overhed pensampelan", "potongan wayar" and "qubit ancilla" are correct, consistent domain renderings. The defects are cosmetic-terminological: "circuit" is left as bare English mid-sentence AND mis-cased throughout — "Cipta Circuit dan observable", "Circuit ini boleh dipisahkan", "Gambar rajah Circuit kuantum" — where standard Malay technical writing uses "litar (kuantum)"; worse, "subcircuit" surfaces as the camelCase artefact "subCircuit" ("4 qubit setiap subCircuit", "kepada subCircuit dan subobservable"), which no native writer would produce. "Backend" is likewise capitalised mid-sentence ("dijalankan pada Backend"). Finally the Step 2 heading "Langkah 2: Optima" uses a non-verb form; the Qiskit-pattern stage verb should read "Optimumkan" (and, for parallelism, "Langkah 1: Petakan" rather than the noun "Peta"). None of this would mislead a learner — the concepts stay identifiable — but an editor would fix all three.

examples.source: Create a circuit and observables / … 4 qubits per subcircuit … / Partition the circuit and observables into subcircuits and subobservables.
examples.suggested: Cipta litar dan observable / … 4 qubit setiap sublitar … / Bahagikan litar dan observable kepada sublitar dan subobservable.
examples.translation: Cipta Circuit dan observable / … 4 qubit setiap subCircuit … / Bahagikan Circuit dan observable kepada subCircuit dan subobservable.
examples.why: "Circuit" is kept in English and capitalised mid-sentence although Malay has the settled term "litar"; "subCircuit" is a camelCase artefact of a find-and-replace, not a word. Meaning survives, so this is MINOR, but it reads as machine output rather than native technical prose.

examples.source: ## Step 2: Optimize
examples.suggested: ## Langkah 2: Optimumkan
examples.translation: ## Langkah 2: Optima
examples.why: The Qiskit-pattern stage names are imperative verbs. "Optima" is not a Malay verb form (Malay has "optimum" / "optimumkan"), so the heading reads as a truncated loan. Step 1 has the same parallelism slip: the noun "Peta" where the verb "Petakan" is meant.

examples.source: #### Generate the experiments to run on the backend.
examples.suggested: #### Jana eksperimen untuk dijalankan pada backend.
examples.translation: #### Jana eksperimen untuk dijalankan pada Backend.
examples.why: Keeping "backend" in English is the right call for the domain, but the mid-sentence capital "Backend" turns a common noun into what looks like a product name — a leftover of the same glossary-substitution pass that produced "Circuit"/"subCircuit".

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — no inversions, no swapped quantities, the Premium/Open-Plan caveat and the `Session`→job-mode workaround, the $b_i=0$ / $Q_{ij}=1$ unweighted simplification, and the 5-node vs 100-node scaling are all carried over correctly — but the terminology is split by an unresolved glossary leak. "circuit" appears both as the proper Malay "litar" ("Asas litar kuantum", "Bina litar ansatz QAOA", "litar ansatz terparameter") and as a bare capitalised English "Circuit" mid-sentence in at least six places ("melaksanakan Circuit di sana", "Transpilkan Circuit abstrak", "parameter yang lebih baik untuk Circuit", "pengoptimuman Circuit"); "session" is likewise split between "**session** Qiskit Runtime" / "[session](...)" and the correct "sesi" (used in the learning outcomes and in Step 3 of the large-scale section), and "backend" surfaces as capitalised "Backend" in prose. Separately, "A noisy, non-monotonic curve" is rendered "Lengkung yang **berbunyi** dan tidak monoton" — "berbunyi" means audible/makes-a-sound, a false friend, while the very same paragraph correctly uses "hingar" for the hardware noise; and "brute-force" becomes the calque "secara kekerasan". None of these teach a false concept, but a native technical editor would fix all of them.

examples.source: the code selects a backend with 127 or more qubits and executes the circuit there.
examples.suggested: kod ini memilih backend dengan 127 atau lebih qubit dan melaksanakan litar tersebut di sana.
examples.translation: kod ini memilih Backend dengan 127 atau lebih qubit dan melaksanakan Circuit di sana.
examples.why: 'circuit' is rendered as the Malay 'litar' in headings and in the ansatz sentences but as a bare capitalised English 'Circuit' in at least six running-prose sentences (and 'backend' as 'Backend'). Within-file inconsistency and an obvious untranslated-glossary artifact; the concept stays identifiable, so MINOR.

examples.source: This iterative loop runs within a Qiskit Runtime **session** ... The QAOA optimization loop runs inside a Qiskit Runtime [session]
examples.suggested: ... berjalan dalam **sesi** Qiskit Runtime ...
examples.translation: Gelung iteratif ini berjalan dalam **session** Qiskit Runtime ... berjalan dalam [session](/guides/execution-modes) Qiskit Runtime
examples.why: The same term is 'sesi' in the learning outcomes, the plan-access note and Step 3 of the large-scale section, but left as English 'session' in the two Background/Step-3 sentences that first introduce it — the least consistent place to leave it.

examples.source: A noisy, non-monotonic curve usually indicates that something upstream needs attention
examples.suggested: Lengkung yang berhingar (bising) dan tidak monoton biasanya menunjukkan ada sesuatu di hulu yang memerlukan perhatian
examples.translation: Lengkung yang berbunyi dan tidak monoton biasanya menunjukkan sesuatu di hulu memerlukan perhatian
examples.why: 'berbunyi' is the acoustic sense of noise ('makes a sound'), a false friend here; the same paragraph already uses the correct signal-sense term 'hingar' twice ('hingar perkakasan', 'hingar sederhana'), so it also contradicts itself.

examples.source: the true optimum is easy to brute-force
examples.suggested: optimum sebenar mudah dicari secara cuba-jaya menyeluruh (brute force)
examples.translation: optimum sebenar mudah dicari secara kekerasan
examples.why: 'kekerasan' means violence/hardness in Malay; as a rendering of computational 'brute force' it is a literal calque no Malay technical writer would produce.

examples.source: After completing this tutorial, you can expect to understand the following information:
examples.suggested: Selepas melengkapkan tutorial ini, anda dijangka dapat memahami perkara berikut:
examples.translation: Selepas melengkapkan tutorial ini, anda boleh mengharapkan untuk memahami maklumat berikut:
examples.why: 'boleh mengharapkan untuk memahami' is a word-for-word calque of 'can expect to understand'; 'mengharapkan' (to hope for) does not carry the English 'expect' sense here, and the construction reads as machine output in an otherwise fluent file.

editor_note: The prose itself is genuinely good, idiomatic Polish with the informal "ty" register held throughout ("Pamiętaj jednak", "znalazłeś(-aś)", "zostaniesz poproszony(-a)"), and the mathematical argument is faithful — but the file is peppered with untranslated/uninflected English terminology that no Polish technical writer would leave. "circuit" appears as raw, uninflected "Circuit" in at least seven places ("Optymalizacja Circuit do uruchomienia", "Wykonanie Circuit na komputerze kwantowym", "za pomocą Circuit kwantowego", "musimy zbudować Circuit implementujący") while the same word is correctly rendered "obwód kwantowy" elsewhere (lines 369, 673, 362) and once as "Układ (Circuit)" (line 247); "qubit" is written as capitalized "Qubit" glued into Polish compounds ("wieloQubitowego", "czteroQubitowy", "Qubitów sterujących") everywhere except line 822, which correctly says "kubitów sterujących". Three section headings were never translated at all ("### The algorithm", "### The hard part: order finding", "### Check your understanding" twice), and "bitstrings" and "Backend" are left as bare English nouns. Smaller defects: a grammar typo "Będą to nietrywialnie czynniki $N$" (should be "nietrywialne"); the train-ride answer collapses into a tautology, "o godzinie 20:00, czyli o 20:00 wieczorem", where the English contrasts 20:00 with 8 PM; QPE is named three different ways ("Kwantowe Szacowanie Fazy", "Kwantowa Estymacja Fazy", untranslated "Quantum Phase Estimation"); and the English sentence "So, the only step that actually needs the power of a quantum computer is the order-finding step" is dropped, leaving "Mówimy zatem, że problem rozkładu na czynniki »redukuje się«…" without the premise it follows from. Nothing here teaches a false concept, so this is not a FAIL, but a native editor would rewrite a lot of it.

examples.source: 2. Optimize the circuit to be run on quantum hardware / 3. Execute your circuit on the quantum computer
examples.suggested: 2. Optymalizacja obwodu pod kątem uruchomienia na sprzęcie kwantowym / 3. Wykonanie obwodu na komputerze kwantowym
examples.translation: 2. Optymalizacja Circuit do uruchomienia na sprzęcie kwantowym / 3. Wykonanie Circuit na komputerze kwantowym
examples.why: "circuit" is left as an uninflected English noun in at least seven places (also "zakodować Circuit", "Circuit z $M_2$", "za pomocą Circuit kwantowego"), which is ungrammatical in Polish, while the very same file uses the correct "obwód kwantowy" at lines 369, 673 and 362, and "Układ (Circuit)" at line 247 — three renderings of one core term.

examples.source: the top $m$ control qubits … four-qubit basis state … four qubits are required
examples.suggested: górne $m$ kubitów sterujących … czterokubitowy stan bazowy … cztery kubity
examples.translation: Górne $m$ Qubitów sterujących … czteroQubitowy stan bazowy … cztery Qubity
examples.why: "qubit" is capitalized as "Qubit" and welded into Polish compounds ("wieloQubitowego", "czteroQubitowy", "Qubitu") — a glossary-leak artifact that looks like mid-word shouting; line 822 shows the correct native form "kubitów sterujących", so the file contradicts itself. Control qubits are also split between "sterujących" and "kontrolnych" (lines 529, 535).

examples.source: Step 4, finding the GCD of two integers, is actually a pretty easy thing to do classically. So, the only step that actually needs the power of a quantum computer is the order-finding step. We say that the factoring problem "reduces" to the order-finding problem.
examples.suggested: … jest natomiast klasycznie dość prostym zadaniem. Jedynym krokiem, który naprawdę wymaga mocy komputera kwantowego, jest zatem wyznaczanie rzędu. Mówimy więc, że problem faktoryzacji „redukuje się" do problemu wyznaczania rzędu.
examples.translation: Krok 4, czyli znalezienie NWD dwóch liczb całkowitych, jest natomiast klasycznie dość prostym zadaniem. Mówimy zatem, że problem rozkładu na czynniki „redukuje się" do problemu wyznaczania rzędu.
examples.why: The sentence carrying the paragraph's punchline is dropped, so the concluding "Mówimy zatem" no longer follows from anything — the learner loses the explicit statement of which single step needs quantum hardware.

examples.source: So, you would arrive at your destination at 20:00, or 8 PM.
examples.suggested: Dotrzesz więc do celu o godzinie 20:00, czyli o 8 wieczorem.
examples.translation: Dotrzesz więc do celu o godzinie 20:00, czyli o 20:00 wieczorem.
examples.why: The English glosses the 24-hour result into the 12-hour clock; the Polish restates 20:00 as "20:00 wieczorem", producing an empty tautology and losing the point of the gloss.

examples.source: These will be nontrivial factors of $N$. … John Watrous' lesson … we start with a unitary $U$ and an eigenstate of that unitary
examples.suggested: Będą to nietrywialne czynniki $N$. … lekcji Johna Watrousa … zaczynamy od operatora unitarnego $U$ oraz stanu własnego tego operatora
examples.translation: Będą to nietrywialnie czynniki $N$. … lekcji Johna Watrouca … zaczynamy od unitarnego operatora $U$ oraz własnego stanu tego unitarnego
examples.why: "nietrywialnie" is an adverb where an adjective is required; the surname is declined wrongly ("Watrouca" instead of "Watrousa"); and "własnego stanu" inverts the fixed Polish term "stan własny" (eigenstate) into "one's own state" — the rest of the file uses "stan własny"/"stanami własnymi" correctly.

editor_note: The running prose is genuinely good Polish — the Theory, geometric-picture and Minesweeper sections read naturally, keep the informal "ty" throughout, and I found no semantic drift (the (2t+1)θ≈π/2 discussion, the "increasing |A_1| decreases t" answer, the 10%-chance caveat, the "101 → mines at x_0 and x_2" conclusion and the "too many iterations rotate past |A_1⟩" warning all match the English exactly). What a native technical editor would fix is a layer of glossary-leak damage sitting on top of that prose. "Circuit" is left in English and uninflected in at least eight prose sentences ("Chcemy Circuit, który działa na stanie…", "Zobaczmy, jaki Circuit został stworzony", "transpilacji naszego Circuitu", "listy Circuit(ów) kwantowych"), splitting the core term against the "obwód" used everywhere else; "Backend" is likewise left bare and uninflected ("dla wybranego Backend", "dla docelowego Backend"). "Qubit" is capitalized mid-sentence throughout and even mid-word ("bramki dwuQubitowe", "liczba Qubitów") while the same sentences also use lowercase "qubit", there is an outright typo "wszystkie Quibty" (line 316), "Primityw środowiska uruchomieniowego `Sampler`" (line 67) is both misspelled and inconsistent with "prymitywów Qiskit Runtime" used later, and line 67 also has the ungrammatical "konstruować wyroczni Grovera" (should be "wyrocznie"). Lines 683–684 leave "qubit" uninflected in Polish case slots ("wszystkie qubit zaangażowane w sterowanie", "na danym qubit", "do tego qubit"), which reads as broken. Smaller splits: "marked" is rendered both zaznaczony (Activity 1/Theory) and oznaczony (Activity 2/summary), "activity" as both aktywność and ćwiczenie, and the same heading appears as "Sprawdź swoje rozumienie" (126) and "Sprawdź swoje zrozumienie" (517, 656). None of this misleads a learner, but all of it is machine-fingerprint that should be cleaned.

examples.source: Thus, we want a circuit $Z_f$ that accomplishes
examples.suggested: Chcemy zatem obwód $Z_f$, który realizuje
examples.translation: Chcemy zatem Circuit $Z_f$, który realizuje
examples.why: 'Circuit' is left in English and uninflected in ~8 prose sentences, splitting the file's core term against 'obwód', which is used correctly dozens of times elsewhere (including two lines earlier). Polish also cannot inflect it, producing 'naszego Circuitu' and 'listy Circuit(ów) kwantowych'.

examples.source: Now we use a preset pass manager to optimize our quantum circuit for the backend we selected.
examples.suggested: …aby zoptymalizować nasz obwód kwantowy dla wybranego backendu.
examples.translation: …aby zoptymalizować nasz obwód kwantowy dla wybranego Backend.
examples.why: 'Backend' is a term the Polish field keeps in English, but it must be declined ('backendu'); left capitalized and uninflected it reads as an untranslated placeholder rather than a Polish sentence. Same defect at line 841 ('dla docelowego Backend').

examples.source: Recall that the MCMTGate flips the sign on a state if and only if all qubits involved in the control are in the $|1\rangle$ state. … If your target has a $|0\rangle$ on a particular qubit … you need to apply an `X` gate to that qubit
examples.suggested: …gdy wszystkie kubity biorące udział w sterowaniu znajdują się w stanie $|1\rangle$. … musisz zastosować bramkę `X` do tego kubitu w wyroczni
examples.translation: …gdy wszystkie qubit zaangażowane w sterowanie znajdują się w stanie $|1\rangle$. … musisz zastosować bramkę `X` do tego qubit w wyroczni
examples.why: 'qubit' is dropped uninflected into nominative-plural, locative and accusative slots, producing three ungrammatical phrases in one bullet list. A native writer would decline the term (kubity / kubicie / kubitu) or at minimum keep it declined in the borrowed form.

examples.source: Here, we demonstrate how to construct Grover oracles … The runtime `Sampler` primitive allows seamless execution of Grover circuits.
examples.suggested: Tutaj pokazujemy, jak konstruować wyrocznie Grovera … Prymityw `Sampler` z Qiskit Runtime umożliwia bezproblemowe wykonywanie obwodów Grovera.
examples.translation: Tutaj pokazujemy, jak konstruować wyroczni Grovera … Primityw środowiska uruchomieniowego `Sampler` umożliwia bezproblemowe wykonywanie obwodów Grovera.
examples.why: Two defects in one sentence: 'wyroczni' is the wrong case (genitive where accusative plural 'wyrocznie' is required), and 'Primityw' is misspelled ('prymityw') as well as inconsistent with 'prymitywów Qiskit Runtime' used in the Step 3 headings and body.

examples.source: …apply a Z gate controlled by all qubits … especially two-qubit gates … repeated the first activity with 20 qubits
examples.suggested: …kontrolowaną przez wszystkie kubity … zwłaszcza bramki dwukubitowe … z 20 kubitami
examples.translation: …kontrolowaną przez wszystkie Quibty … zwłaszcza bramki dwuQubitowe … z 20 Qubitami
examples.why: 'Qubit' is capitalized mid-sentence throughout the file and even mid-compound ('dwuQubitowe'), while the same paragraphs use lowercase 'qubit' ('każdy qubit', 'qubit 0'); line 316 additionally contains the typo 'Quibty'. This is a glossary-leak artifact, not a Polish convention.

examples.source: Check your understanding / marked states / activity
examples.suggested: Pick one rendering per term: „Sprawdź swoje zrozumienie", „stany oznaczone", „aktywność".
examples.translation: „Sprawdź swoje rozumienie" vs „Sprawdź swoje zrozumienie"; „zaznaczonych stanów" vs „oznaczonych stanów"; „aktywność" vs „ćwiczenie"
examples.why: Three within-file splits of repeated labels/terms — the identical English heading is rendered two ways, 'marked' alternates between zaznaczony (Theory/Activity 1) and oznaczony (Activity 2/summary), and 'activity' between aktywność (headings) and ćwiczenie (body). Recognizable, but it undercuts the teaching material's consistency.

editor_note: The running prose is fluent and idiomatic PT (informal "você"/imperative throughout: "Construa seu primeiro...", "Veja seus resultados mudarem"), and no meaning is inverted or dropped — but a glossary keep-English rule has leaked into the body text. "circuit" is never translated and is capitalized mid-sentence in five places ("um Circuit quântico", "Construa seu Circuit", "ao final do Circuit", "executar um Circuit em hardware quântico real"); the standard, unambiguous PT term is "circuito (quântico)". The same leak capitalizes "Qubit/Qubits" and "Gate CX" in the section-4 bullet, where PT convention is lowercase "qubit" and "porta CX" (or at least lowercase "gate CX"); note the file itself already uses lowercase Portuguese elsewhere ("hardware quântico", "medições"), so the capitals read as machine artifacts rather than a deliberate convention. Separately, the "Next steps" link label is stale: EN reads "the Run your first circuit on hardware guide" while PT still says "Siga os passos em [Hello world]" (the old EN page title) — the target URL is correct, so it misdirects nobody, but the visible label no longer matches the source. Entanglement is rendered consistently as "entrelaçado/entrelaçamento", a defensible and internally consistent choice, so it is not counted as a defect.

examples.source: Build your first quantum circuit in under two minutes, on your local environment
examples.suggested: Construa seu primeiro circuito quântico em menos de dois minutos, no seu ambiente local
examples.translation: Construa seu primeiro Circuit quântico em menos de dois minutos, no seu ambiente local
examples.why: "circuit" is left in English and capitalized mid-sentence in five places, including the frontmatter description and the H2 "Construa seu Circuit". Portuguese has the fully standard "circuito quântico"; keeping the English noun here is a glossary keep-English leak, not a field convention (unlike qubit/shots).

examples.source: Add a third qubit by changing to `QuantumCircuit(3)`, and add a second CX gate ... all three of these qubits have been entangled.
examples.suggested: Adicione um terceiro qubit alterando para `QuantumCircuit(3)` e adicione uma segunda porta CX ... todos os três qubits foram entrelaçados.
examples.translation: Adicione um terceiro Qubit alterando para `QuantumCircuit(3)`, e adicione um segundo Gate CX ... todos os três Qubits foram entrelaçados.
examples.why: "qubit" is correctly kept in English but wrongly capitalized as a proper noun mid-sentence, and "gate" is left untranslated as "Gate CX" where PT technical writing says "porta CX". Recognizable, so not misleading, but no native technical writer would capitalize these.

examples.source: Follow the steps in the [Run your first circuit on hardware](/guides/hello-world) guide to run a circuit on real quantum hardware.
examples.suggested: Siga os passos no guia [Execute seu primeiro circuito em hardware](/guides/hello-world) para executar um circuito em hardware quântico real.
examples.translation: Siga os passos em [Hello world](/guides/hello-world) para executar um Circuit em hardware quântico real.
examples.why: The visible link label still carries the old EN page title "Hello world" instead of the current "Run your first circuit on hardware"; the URL is right so nobody is sent astray, but the label no longer matches the page it points to and the word "guia" was dropped.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — the stretch resolution rule ("qualquer resto ... é adicionado ao primeiro delay que usa o stretch"), the 25-with-remainder-1 example, the barrier-region and non-negativity constraints all match the English, and the informal "você" register holds. The defects are glossary leaks and inconsistency: "circuit" is rendered three ways in the same file — "circuito" (paragraphs under Desacoplamento dinâmico), capitalized English "Circuit" ("após o Circuit ser escalonado", "tempo total do Circuit", "Visualizar temporização do Circuit"), and the hybrid "sub-Circuit" — while the frontmatter description still says "circuits dinâmicos". "gate" is likewise split between "porta/portas" and capitalized "Gate" ("quando o Gate `x` começa"), and "qubit" between lowercase "qubit" and capitalized "Qubits" ("conjunto de Qubits ... um ou mais Qubits"). The opening paragraph also carries two gender-agreement errors, "dos portas calibrados" and "aplicação de um porta" (porta is feminine: "das portas calibradas", "de uma porta"), plus the calque "expressar designs de porta" where a native writer would say "projetar sequências de portas".

examples.source: applying a gate for the duration of some sub-circuit / after the circuit is scheduled / the total circuit time / Visualize circuit timing
examples.suggested: aplicação de uma porta pela duração de algum subcircuito / após o circuito ser escalonado / o tempo total do circuito / Visualizar temporização do circuito
examples.translation: aplicação de um porta pela duração de algum sub-Circuit / após o Circuit ser escalonado / o tempo total do Circuit / Visualizar temporização do Circuit
examples.why: The file already uses the correct Portuguese "circuito" elsewhere ("O circuito correspondente seria como o seguinte"); the capitalized English "Circuit"/"sub-Circuit" is an untranslated glossary leak and makes the same concept look like two different things.

examples.source: after the exact duration of calibrated gates are known
examples.suggested: após serem conhecidas as durações exatas das portas calibradas
examples.translation: após as durações exatas dos portas calibrados serem conhecidas
examples.why: "porta" is feminine in Portuguese, so "dos portas calibrados" is a double gender-agreement error no native technical writer would produce; the postposed "serem conhecidas" is also stiff calqued syntax.

examples.source: when the `x` gate starts / per _qubit set_ ... A qubit set is one or more qubits
examples.suggested: quando a porta `x` começa / por _conjunto de qubits_ ... Um conjunto de qubits é composto por um ou mais qubits
examples.translation: quando o Gate `x` começa / por _conjunto de Qubits_ ... Um conjunto de Qubits é composto por um ou mais Qubits
examples.why: Same terms are rendered lowercase-Portuguese earlier in the file ("sequência de portas", "um qubit ocioso"); the mid-file switch to capitalized English "Gate"/"Qubits" is an inconsistency, and the English source uses lowercase "qubit" here anyway.

examples.source: You can then express gate designs such as evenly spacing gates / The requested goal value / depend on the goal value
examples.suggested: Você pode então projetar sequências de portas, como espaçar portas uniformemente / O valor-alvo solicitado / dependem do valor-alvo
examples.translation: Você pode então expressar designs de porta como espaçamento uniforme de portas / O valor de meta solicitado / dependem do valor de meta
examples.why: "expressar designs de porta" is a word-for-word calque of "express gate designs", and "valor de meta" is a literal rendering where Portuguese technical writing says "valor-alvo"; both are understandable but read as machine output.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — no drift, no dropped caveats, informal "tu" register holds ("consultă", "Mapează", "Taie", "Rulează") — but the prose carries a German-style mid-sentence capitalization of common nouns that Romanian orthography does not allow: "numărul de Qubiți dintr-un Circuit", "Vom tăia Gate-uri", "un Backend fals", "Circuitele cu Backend-ul nostru". A native technical editor would lowercase all of these. The same words are also inconsistent within the file: "circuite și operatori cuantici" / "un circuit cuantic" (lines 17–18) are lowercase while "Circuit" is capitalized everywhere else. Separately, "sampling overhead" is rendered "supraîncărcare de eșantionare" — "supraîncărcare" means overload/overloading, not the multiplicative sampling cost; "cost suplimentar de eșantionare" (or keeping "overhead") is the conventional rendering. Recognizable, not misleading, hence MINOR.

examples.source: …while using **circuit cutting** to reduce the number of qubits in a circuit. We will cut gates to enable us to reconstruct the expectation value of a four-qubit circuit…
examples.suggested: …pentru a reduce numărul de qubiți dintr-un circuit. Vom tăia porți (gates) pentru a putea reconstrui valoarea de așteptare a unui circuit de patru qubiți…
examples.translation: …folosind **circuit cutting** pentru a reduce numărul de Qubiți dintr-un Circuit. Vom tăia Gate-uri pentru a putea reconstrui valoarea de așteptare a unui Circuit de patru Qubiți…
examples.why: Romanian does not capitalize common nouns mid-sentence; "Qubiți / Circuit / Gate-uri" reads as a German-orthography calque and marks the text as machine-produced, even though the meaning is correct. Same pattern at lines 20, 58, 98, 112, 116, 126, 128, 136, 138, 198.

examples.source: Calculate the sampling overhead for the chosen cuts … the sampling overhead incurred by circuit cutting
examples.suggested: Calcularea costului suplimentar de eșantionare (sampling overhead) pentru tăieturile alese … costul suplimentar de eșantionare generat de circuit cutting
examples.translation: Calcularea supraîncărcării de eșantionare pentru tăieturile alese … supraîncărcarea de eșantionare generată de circuit cutting
examples.why: "Supraîncărcare" is Romanian for overload/overburdening, not for the overhead factor (here 9² = 81 extra samples). The reader can still infer "extra cost" from context, so it is imperfect-but-recognizable rather than false, but it is not the conventional domain rendering.

examples.source: Map problem to quantum circuits and operators / Map the hamiltonian onto a quantum circuit.
examples.suggested: Use one convention for "circuit" across the file (lowercase "circuit" everywhere).
examples.translation: Maparea problemei pe circuite și operatori cuantici / Mapează hamiltonianul pe un circuit cuantic.
examples.why: Within-file inconsistency: "circuit(e)" is lowercase in the Step-1 bullets but capitalized as "Circuit" in the intro and in every later section ("Crearea unui Circuit de tăiat", "Circuitului de dimensiune completă"). The concept stays identifiable, so this is MINOR, but the split makes the page look unedited.

editor_note: No semantic drift: the technical content (MPF definition, static-MPF/LSE explanation, the "remaining Trotter error is smaller than with the largest k_j" claim, the closing caveat that the approximate model came out worse than the exact solution) is faithful, and the informal "tu" register holds throughout ("vei învăța", "poți folosi", "Reține că ai libertate deplină"). What a Romanian editor would fix is terminology hygiene: lattice "sites" is rendered "site-uri", which in Romanian reads as *websites* — the physics term is "situri" ("o linie de 10 situri"). "Circuit" appears in four shapes within the file — "Circuit Trotter", "Circuit-urile", "circuit-uri", "circuitele" — with a stray mid-sentence capital that also hits "10 Qubiți" (should be lowercase "qubiți"), glossary-protection residue rather than Romanian orthography. "Qiskit pattern" is "pattern Qiskit" at the top but silently becomes "pasul din tipar" in Step 2. Two smaller prose issues: "a rezultat de fapt într-o valoare așteptată mai proastă" calques English "resulted in" (Romanian: "a condus la"), and "Ca indicator al faptului că un MPF ... va produce rezultate bune" turns the English "as an indicator *whether* ... will yield good results" into an assertion that it will.

examples.source: We use the Ising model on a line of 10 sites: ... where $J$ is the coupling strength between two sites
examples.suggested: Folosim modelul Ising pe o linie de 10 situri: ... intensitatea cuplajului dintre două situri
examples.translation: Folosim modelul Ising pe o linie de 10 site-uri: ... intensitatea cuplajului dintre două site-uri
examples.why: In Romanian, "site-uri" is the everyday word for websites; the lattice-site term in spin-model/solid-state literature is "situri" (sg. "sit"). Recoverable from context, but wrong-domain vocabulary in a physics text.

examples.source: the deepest Trotter circuit ... the Trotterized time-evolution circuits ... we transpile our circuits ... several shorter-depth circuits ... a simple line of 10 qubits
examples.suggested: circuitul Trotter cel mai adânc ... circuitele de evoluție temporală Trotterizate ... transpilăm circuitele noastre ... circuite adânci ... mai multe circuite cu adâncime mai mică ... o linie simplă de 10 qubiți
examples.translation: cel mai adânc Circuit Trotter ... Circuit-urile de evoluție temporală Trotterizate ... transpilăm Circuit-urile noastre ... circuit-uri adânci ... mai multe Circuit-uri cu adâncime mai mică ... circuitele cuantice Trotterizate ... o linie simplă de 10 Qubiți
examples.why: One common noun is spelled four ways in the same file ("Circuit", "Circuit-uri", "circuit-uri", "circuitele"). Romanian inflects "circuit" natively (circuite/circuitele); the hyphen and the mid-sentence capital are glossary-protection residue. Same defect on "10 Qubiți", which should be lowercase.

examples.source: working through the steps of a **Qiskit pattern** ... this is the step in the pattern during which you optimize your circuits
examples.suggested: ... acesta este pasul din pattern-ul Qiskit în care îți optimizezi circuitele
examples.translation: parcurgând pașii unui **pattern Qiskit** ... acesta este pasul din tipar în care îți optimizezi circuitele
examples.why: "Qiskit pattern" is a named Qiskit concept introduced in English at the top, then re-rendered as the generic Romanian "tipar" 270 lines later; the reader must infer that "tipar" is the same thing.

examples.source: As an indicator whether an MPF constructed with these coefficients will yield good results, we can use the L1-norm.
examples.suggested: Pentru a evalua dacă un MPF construit cu acești coeficienți va produce rezultate bune, putem folosi norma L1.
examples.translation: Ca indicator al faptului că un MPF construit cu acești coeficienți va produce rezultate bune, putem folosi norma L1.
examples.why: The English frames the L1-norm as a diagnostic of *whether* the result will be good; "al faptului că" presupposes it will be, flattening the point the next section makes (that the norm can come out too high).

examples.source: since it actually resulted in an expectation value that is worse than the exact solution
examples.suggested: deoarece a condus de fapt la o valoare așteptată mai proastă decât soluția exactă
examples.translation: deoarece a rezultat de fapt într-o valoare așteptată mai proastă decât soluția exactă
examples.why: "a rezultat în" is a direct calque of English "resulted in"; Romanian uses "a condus la" / "a dus la". Grammatical, but clearly translated rather than written.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — the load-bearing negation in "MPF แบบ _static_ คือ MPF ที่ค่า $x_j$ **ไม่** ขึ้นกับเวลา evolution" is intact, and the closing caveat that the approximate model gave a worse expectation value than the exact solution is preserved — so nothing here misleads a learner. What a native editor would change: (1) "expectation value" is split within the file between "ค่าคาดหวัง" (the Step-4 bullet, line 25) and "ค่าความคาดหวัง" (lines 296, 308, 319, 354), and the Step headings are split between Thai "ขั้นตอนที่ 1" (line 26) and untranslated "Step 2 / Step 3 / Step 4" (lines 279, 294, 306), with "Reconstruct results" rendered "สร้างผลลัพธ์ใหม่" in the bullet but "สร้างผลลัพธ์" in the heading. (2) Two clear calques: "ค่าที่เล็กที่สุดมีแรงบันดาลใจจาก..." for "is motivated by" (literally "is inspired by", line 142) and "นี่คือขั้นตอนในรูปแบบที่..." for "the step in the pattern" (line 281), which severs the link to "Qiskit pattern" kept in English at line 15. (3) Small dropped qualifiers: "on our observable" is gone from the opening sentence (line 14), and "than other choices" is gone from line 138, leaving "การขยายสัญญาณรบกวนที่มากกว่า" with no comparand. Collocations "ความแข็งแกร่งของการคัปปลิง" (coupling strength) and "สัมประสิทธิ์การขยาย" (expansion coefficients, line 245) are recognizable but not the natural Thai physics/maths collocations.

examples.source: Compute the MPF expectation value / expectation values
examples.suggested: Pick one rendering (ค่าคาดหวัง) and use it in all five places
examples.translation: คำนวณค่าคาดหวัง MPF … ค่าความคาดหวังของ observable เป้าหมาย … ค่าความคาดหวังรวมของ MPF
examples.why: The same core term 'expectation value' is rendered two ways inside one short file; both are recognizable so it does not mislead, but a technical editor would unify it.

examples.source: The smallest value is motivated by the target evolution time of $t=8.0$
examples.suggested: ค่าที่เล็กที่สุดมาจาก/กำหนดโดยเวลา evolution เป้าหมาย $t=8.0$
examples.translation: ค่าที่เล็กที่สุดมีแรงบันดาลใจจากเวลา evolution เป้าหมาย $t=8.0$
examples.why: 'มีแรงบันดาลใจจาก' is 'is inspired by' — a word-for-word calque of 'motivated by'. No Thai technical writer would say a numeric choice is 'inspired'; it reads as MT in an otherwise fluent passage.

examples.source: but some $k_j$'s will lead to a larger noise amplification on real devices than other choices
examples.suggested: …การขยายสัญญาณรบกวนบนอุปกรณ์จริงมากกว่าค่าอื่นๆ
examples.translation: แต่บาง $k_j$ จะนำไปสู่การขยายสัญญาณรบกวนที่มากกว่าบนอุปกรณ์จริง
examples.why: The comparand 'than other choices' is dropped, leaving 'ที่มากกว่า' hanging with nothing to compare against. The point (that the choice of k_j is what varies noise) is still inferable, so it is a dropped qualifier rather than a semantic inversion.

examples.source: Normally, this is the step in the pattern during which you optimize your circuits for execution on hardware.
examples.suggested: โดยปกติ นี่คือขั้นตอนของ Qiskit pattern ที่เราปรับแต่ง Circuit ให้พร้อมรันบนฮาร์ดแวร์
examples.translation: โดยปกติ นี่คือขั้นตอนในรูปแบบที่เราปรับแต่ง Circuit ให้พร้อมรันบนฮาร์ดแวร์
examples.why: 'ในรูปแบบ' literally translates 'in the pattern' but reads as generic 'in the format', breaking the reference to the 'Qiskit pattern' that was deliberately kept in English at the top of the page; the pedagogical thread of the four-step pattern is weakened.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — the physics chain (viscous → ν=0 → conservation equation → shock waves → inviscid Burgers'), the 13-vs-3021/4701 parameter comparison, the 28-iteration/0.0015 loss claim, the >70% aerodynamics figure and the `initialization="RANDOM"` caveat all survive intact, and the English-loan convention (Qubit, Circuit, Backend, solver, convergence, inviscid/viscous, PINN) is applied consistently, so nothing here misleads. What a native technical editor would change is word-level: `strategy` is transliterated as "สตราเทอีจี", a malformed non-word (Thai uses "กลยุทธ์", or simply leaves "strategy"); the "Background" heading is rendered "พื้นหลัง", the visual-backdrop sense, where a document section needs "ความเป็นมา"/"ภูมิหลัง"; "the infinitesimal effect of transport" becomes "ผลกระทบของการขนส่ง", the logistics/shipping word rather than the fluid-transport sense ("การถ่ายเท"/"การส่งผ่าน"); and "coupled" PDEs becomes "มีการจับคู่กัน" (pairing/matching) instead of "ที่เชื่อมโยงกัน"/"ควบคู่กัน".
